days.title: El presente irregular, todo junto
days.objective: The learner can recall and correctly conjugate the four families of stem-changing verbs and the key multi-irregular verbs (oír, venir, decir, tener) in the present tense without hesitating over which pattern applies.
days.paretoFocus: Fluent present-tense speech depends on instant recall of these irregular patterns, which appear in almost every daily sentence a beginner needs.
drills: Write out the present tense of pensar, volver, pedir and hacer in one sitting.
Say aloud five sentences using tener, venir, decir and oír about your own day.
Sort querer, dormir, servir and salir into their irregularity family from memory.

items: Recall the o>ue stem change in a verb like poder.
Recall how to say what you are going to do tomorrow with ir a.
Recall the difference in meaning between tener que and hay que.

activities.title: Las familias del presente irregular
activities.intro: This lesson gathers the irregular present tense you already know into one table and adds four verbs that break more than one rule at once: oír, venir, decir and tener.

items.hr: Pienso, piensas, piensa, pensamos, pensáis, piensan.
items.en: I think, you think, he/she thinks, we think, you all think, they think.
items.note: e>ie: nosotros and vosotros keep the unchanged stem

items.hr: Vuelvo tarde porque duermo poco.
items.en: I get back late because I sleep little.
items.note: o>ue: volver, dormir

items.hr: Pido la cuenta y sigo aquí un rato.
items.en: I ask for the bill and I stay here a while.
items.note: e>i: pedir, seguir

items.hr: Hago la cama y salgo a las ocho.
items.en: I make the bed and I go out at eight.
items.note: yo-form irregular: hago, salgo

items.hr: Oigo, vengo, digo y tengo prisa hoy.
items.en: I hear, I come, I say and I am in a hurry today.
items.note: multi-irregular verbs: oír, venir, decir, tener

activities.title: Las familias, mezcladas
activities.intro: Practise choosing the right irregular present form across all the families at once.

questions.prompt: ¿Cómo se dice 'we prefer' con el verbo preferir?
questions.explanation: nosotros and vosotros keep the unchanged stem in e>ie verbs, so preferir gives preferimos.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma correcta de 'oír' para 'yo'?
questions.explanation: oír adds a g in the yo-form, like tener and salir: oigo.

questions.prompt: Completa: Ana _____ (pedir) un café todos los días.
questions.explanation: pedir is an e>i stem-changing verb: pide.

questions.prompt: Completa: Los sábados yo _____ que limpiar la casa.
questions.explanation: tener que + infinitive expresses personal obligation; tengo is the yo-form of tener.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I hear that you say strange things.'
questions.explanation: oigo (oír) and dices (decir) are both irregular forms used together.

activities.title: Un día ajetreado
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend asks about your day, which is full of irregular verbs.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿A qué hora sales de casa entre semana?
lines.en: What time do you leave the house on weekdays?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Salgo a las ocho, pero hoy vengo tarde.
lines.en: I leave at eight, but today I'm coming late.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Por qué? ¿Qué pasa?
lines.en: Why? What's going on?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Duermo poco y hoy pido el día libre.
lines.en: I sleep little and today I'm asking for the day off.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Entiendo. ¿Vuelves pronto a casa?
lines.en: I understand. Are you coming back home soon?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, vuelvo a las cinco y hago la cena.
lines.en: Yes, I get back at five and I make dinner.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Dices la verdad o tienes otro plan?
lines.en: Are you telling the truth or do you have another plan?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Digo la verdad, tengo mucho trabajo hoy.
lines.en: I'm telling the truth, I have a lot of work today.

days.title: La rutina diaria y los verbos reflexivos
days.objective: The learner can conjugate common reflexive verbs and place the reflexive pronoun correctly before the conjugated verb to describe a daily routine.
days.paretoFocus: Describing your own routine is one of the first things every Spanish course and every real conversation asks for, and it depends entirely on getting the reflexive pronoun in the right place.
drills: Write your real morning routine using five reflexive verbs.
Say aloud the full conjugation of levantarse.
Translate three English routine sentences into Spanish with the pronoun in front of the verb.

items: Recall the four irregular present families from the last lesson.
Recall how to say what time you leave the house.
Recall the yo-form irregular of hacer and salir.

activities.title: Los verbos reflexivos
activities.intro: Reflexive verbs describe actions you do to yourself. The pronoun me, te, se, nos, os or se goes right before the conjugated verb.

items.hr: Me levanto a las siete.
items.en: I get up at seven.
items.note: levantarse: pronoun before the verb

items.hr: Te duchas por la mañana.
items.en: You shower in the morning.
items.note: ducharse: regular -ar reflexive verb

items.hr: Nos vestimos deprisa.
items.en: We get dressed quickly.
items.note: vestirse: e>i stem change plus reflexive pronoun

items.hr: ¿Os acostáis tarde los viernes?
items.en: Do you all go to bed late on Fridays?
items.note: acostarse: o>ue stem change, vosotros form

items.hr: Ana se levanta, se ducha y se viste en media hora.
items.en: Ana gets up, showers and gets dressed in half an hour.
items.note: three reflexive verbs in one sentence

activities.title: La rutina, paso a paso
activities.intro: Practise conjugating reflexive verbs and placing the pronoun correctly.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma correcta para 'tú' de acostarse?
questions.explanation: acostarse is o>ue, and the tú pronoun is te: te acuestas.

questions.prompt: ¿Dónde va el pronombre reflexivo con un verbo conjugado?
questions.explanation: with a conjugated verb, the reflexive pronoun always comes right before it.

questions.prompt: Completa: Nosotros _____ (vestirse) por la mañana.
questions.explanation: vestirse is e>i, and nosotros takes nos: nos vestimos.

questions.prompt: Completa: A mí _____ (gustar) levantarme temprano.
questions.explanation: gustar with a singular infinitive takes the singular form: me gusta.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'We get up early and shower fast.'
questions.explanation: both reflexive verbs need their own pronoun, nos, before each conjugated verb.

activities.title: La rutina de cada día
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk about your daily routine using reflexive verbs.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿A qué hora te levantas entre semana?
lines.en: What time do you get up on weekdays?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Me levanto a las siete y media.
lines.en: I get up at half past seven.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Te duchas por la mañana o por la noche?
lines.en: Do you shower in the morning or at night?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Me ducho por la mañana, y luego me visto rápido.
lines.en: I shower in the morning, and then I get dressed fast.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Os acostáis tarde en tu familia?
lines.en: Do you all go to bed late in your family?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, nos acostamos pronto entre semana.
lines.en: No, we go to bed early on weekdays.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y los fines de semana?
lines.en: And on weekends?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Los fines de semana nos acostamos más tarde.
lines.en: On weekends we go to bed later.

days.title: Verbos pronominales: irse, quedarse, ponerse
days.objective: The learner can recognise and use pseudo-reflexive verbs (irse, quedarse, ponerse, llamarse) and the reciprocal se, where the pronoun does not mean 'to oneself'.
days.paretoFocus: Many of the most frequent Spanish verbs carry a pronoun that changes meaning rather than marking a reflexive action, and misunderstanding this blocks basic comprehension.
drills: List five sentences with irse, quedarse or ponerse about a plan you have.
Explain in your own words why llamarse is not literally 'to call yourself'.
Write one sentence using a reciprocal verb about two people you know.

items: Recall how to conjugate a reflexive verb like levantarse.
Recall where the reflexive pronoun goes in the sentence.
Recall the vosotros form of acostarse.

activities.title: Pronombres que cambian el significado
activities.intro: Some verbs use a pronoun that does not mean 'myself, yourself...': it changes the verb's meaning instead. Others mark a reciprocal action, 'each other'.

items.hr: Me voy, tengo prisa.
items.en: I'm off, I'm in a hurry.
items.note: irse = to leave, go away; different from plain ir

items.hr: ¿Te quedas en casa esta tarde?
items.en: Are you staying home this afternoon?
items.note: quedarse = to stay

items.hr: Me pongo nervioso antes de un examen.
items.en: I get nervous before an exam.
items.note: ponerse + adjective = to become

items.hr: Mi hermano se llama Pablo.
items.en: My brother's name is Pablo.
items.note: llamarse, literally 'to call oneself', used for naming

items.hr: Marta y Luis se conocen del colegio.
items.en: Marta and Luis know each other from school.
items.note: reciprocal se: 'each other'

activities.title: Significados distintos
activities.intro: Practise telling apart these pronominal verbs from a literal reflexive reading.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué significa 'se quedan' en 'Ellos se quedan en el hotel'?
questions.explanation: quedarse here means to stay or lodge somewhere, not a literal reflexive action.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es el significado de 'se conocen' en 'Ana y Pedro se conocen bien'?
options: Se conocen el uno al otro
Ana se conoce a sí misma
questions.answer: Se conocen el uno al otro
questions.explanation: this se is reciprocal: it means 'each other', not 'themselves'.

questions.prompt: Completa: Yo _____ (ponerse) contento cuando viajo.
questions.explanation: ponerse + adjective expresses becoming a state: me pongo contento.

questions.prompt: Completa: Son las cinco _____ media.
questions.explanation: half past the hour is expressed with y media.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I'm leaving, but you can stay.'
questions.explanation: irse (me voy) and quedarse (quedarte) contrast the two pseudo-reflexive meanings.

activities.title: Planes para la tarde
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend is surprised you're leaving so soon.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Te vas ya? Es un poco pronto.
lines.en: Are you leaving already? It's a bit early.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, me voy, tengo que estudiar.
lines.en: Yes, I'm off, I have to study.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Te quedas en casa toda la tarde?
lines.en: Are you staying home all afternoon?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, me quedo una hora y luego salgo.
lines.en: No, I'm staying an hour and then I'm going out.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cómo se llama tu compañera de piso?
lines.en: What's your flatmate's name?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Se llama Elena, nos conocemos de la universidad.
lines.en: Her name is Elena, we know each other from university.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Me pongo un poco triste si te vas tan pronto.
lines.en: I get a little sad if you leave so soon.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No pasa nada, vuelvo mañana.
lines.en: It's fine, I'm coming back tomorrow.

days.title: Estar + gerundio: ahora mismo
days.objective: The learner can form the present progressive with estar plus gerund, including the irregular gerunds leyendo, durmiendo and pidiendo, to describe an action in progress right now.
days.paretoFocus: Distinguishing what happens generally from what is happening right now is a routine real-time need, and the irregular gerunds belong to verbs learners already use every day.
drills: Say five things happening around you right now using estar + gerundio.
Write the gerund of leer, dormir, pedir and decir.
Compare como and estoy comiendo out loud and explain the difference.

items: Recall a reflexive verb you use every morning.
Recall how gustar changes with a plural subject.
Recall the pseudo-reflexive meaning of ponerse.

activities.title: El gerundio y estar
activities.intro: Estar plus the gerund describes an action happening right now. Regular gerunds end in -ando or -iendo; some -ir verbs change their stem vowel in the gerund.

items.hr: Estoy leyendo un libro muy interesante.
items.en: I am reading a very interesting book.
items.note: leer -> leyendo: the i becomes y between vowels

items.hr: Mi hermano está durmiendo todavía.
items.en: My brother is still sleeping.
items.note: dormir -> durmiendo: o becomes u in the gerund

items.hr: ¿Qué estás pidiendo?
items.en: What are you ordering?
items.note: pedir -> pidiendo: e becomes i in the gerund

items.hr: Estamos comiendo en la cocina.
items.en: We are eating in the kitchen.
items.note: regular gerund: -iendo for -er verbs

items.hr: En España decimos 'ya viene'; en parte de América también oyes 'está viniendo'.
items.en: In Spain we say 'ya viene' (he is on his way); in parts of America you also hear 'está viniendo'.
items.note: American Spanish extends the progressive to punctual events; peninsular Spanish does not

activities.title: ¿Qué está pasando ahora?
activities.intro: Practise building and recognising the present progressive.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es el gerundio correcto de 'leer'?
questions.explanation: between two vowels the i of the regular ending becomes y: leyendo.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué frase describe una acción en este momento?
questions.explanation: only estar + gerundio marks an action happening right now.

questions.prompt: Completa: Ellos _____ (dormir, estar + gerundio) la siesta.
questions.explanation: dormir changes o to u in the gerund: durmiendo.

questions.prompt: Completa: A ella _____ (gustar) leer por la noche.
questions.explanation: gustar with a singular infinitive and le (a ella) gives le gusta.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'What are you ordering right now?'
questions.explanation: estás pidiendo is the present progressive of pedir, with e>i in the gerund.

activities.title: ¿Qué estás haciendo?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Describe what is happening right now, including at a bar.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué estás haciendo?
lines.en: What are you doing?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Estoy leyendo un correo del trabajo.
lines.en: I'm reading a work email.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y tu hermana? ¿Está despierta?
lines.en: And your sister? Is she awake?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, todavía está durmiendo.
lines.en: No, she's still sleeping.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: En el bar, ¿qué están pidiendo tus amigos?
lines.en: At the bar, what are your friends ordering?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Están pidiendo café y algo de comer.
lines.en: They're ordering coffee and something to eat.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Aquí está lloviendo todo el día.
lines.en: Here it's been raining all day.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, y está lloviendo mucho ahora mismo.
lines.en: Yes, and it's raining a lot right now.

days.title: Los pronombres de objeto directo
days.objective: The learner can identify and use direct object pronouns (lo, la, los, las, me, te, nos, os) to replace a previously mentioned direct object, placed before the conjugated verb.
days.paretoFocus: Replacing a repeated noun with a pronoun is what makes Spanish sound natural instead of childishly repetitive, and it is required constantly in real answers.
drills: Answer three questions about objects around you using lo, la, los or las instead of repeating the noun.
Write five sentences where you replace a direct object with me, te, nos or os.
Practise saying ¿Lo tienes? and ¿La tienes? about different objects.

items: Recall the gerund of leer, dormir and pedir.
Recall the difference between está lloviendo and llueve.
Recall one sentence using irse or quedarse.

activities.title: Lo, la, los, las
activities.intro: A direct object pronoun replaces the thing or person directly affected by the verb, so you do not repeat the noun. It goes right before the conjugated verb.

items.hr: ¿Tienes las llaves? Sí, las tengo.
items.en: Do you have the keys? Yes, I have them.
items.note: las = feminine plural direct object

items.hr: ¿Ves el coche? No, no lo veo.
items.en: Do you see the car? No, I don't see it.
items.note: lo = masculine singular direct object

items.hr: Compro la fruta y la llevo a casa.
items.en: I buy the fruit and take it home.
items.note: la = feminine singular

items.hr: ¿Nos llamas esta noche?
items.en: Will you call us tonight?
items.note: nos = us, first person plural

items.hr: Te veo mañana en la oficina.
items.en: I'll see you tomorrow at the office.
items.note: te = you, placed before the conjugated verb

activities.title: Sustituir el objeto directo
activities.intro: Practise replacing a direct object noun with its pronoun.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué pronombre sustituye a 'los libros' en '¿Tienes los libros?'?
questions.explanation: los libros is masculine plural, so the pronoun is los.

questions.prompt: Elige la respuesta correcta a '¿Compras la leche?'
questions.explanation: la leche is feminine singular, so the pronoun is la.

questions.prompt: Completa: ¿Ves a Marta? Sí, _____ veo en la calle.
questions.explanation: Marta is a feminine singular direct object, so la.

questions.prompt: Completa: Mañana _____ (ir a) visitar a mis abuelos.
questions.explanation: ir a + infinitive expresses a planned future action: voy a visitar.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I have the tickets and I bring them today.'
questions.explanation: las entradas is replaced by las the second time, to avoid repeating the noun.

activities.title: ¿Dónde están mis cosas?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Help a friend find their things, using direct object pronouns.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Tienes mi móvil? No lo encuentro.
lines.en: Do you have my phone? I can't find it.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, lo tengo aquí, lo siento.
lines.en: Yes, I have it here, sorry.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y mis llaves? ¿Las ves por algún lado?
lines.en: And my keys? Do you see them anywhere?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, las veo, están en la mesa.
lines.en: Yes, I see them, they're on the table.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Compras el pan de camino a casa?
lines.en: Will you buy the bread on the way home?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, lo compro y también compro la fruta.
lines.en: Okay, I'll buy it and I'll also buy the fruit.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Perfecto. Te veo luego, entonces.
lines.en: Perfect. I'll see you later, then.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, nos vemos a las siete.
lines.en: Okay, we'll see each other at seven.

days.title: Los pronombres de objeto indirecto
days.objective: The learner can use the indirect object pronouns le and les correctly, including the redundant doubling Spanish requires when the indirect object is also named, as in Le doy el libro a Ana.
days.paretoFocus: Leaving out the redundant pronoun is the single most common omission English speakers make, and it makes a sentence sound clearly non-native even when every word is otherwise right.
drills: Write three sentences that name the person and also use le or les, like Le escribo un mensaje a mi madre.
Say aloud five sentences with le regalo, le doy, le explico about different people.
Write one English sentence and its Spanish equivalent side by side and notice English marks no doubling at all.

items: Recall how to replace a direct object with lo, la, los or las.
Recall a sentence with me, te, nos or os as a direct object.
Recall the gerund of pedir.

activities.title: Le, les y la duplicación
activities.intro: Le and les mean 'to him/her' and 'to them'. Spanish normally keeps le or les even when the person is also named with a, which English never does.

items.hr: Le doy el libro a Ana.
items.en: I give the book to Ana.
items.note: le = to her; the redundant pronoun is required even though 'a Ana' is also there

items.hr: Les escribo un correo a mis padres.
items.en: I write an email to my parents.
items.note: les = to them

items.hr: ¿Qué le regalas a tu hermano?
items.en: What are you giving your brother?
items.note: le refers forward to 'a tu hermano'

items.hr: Le explico el problema al profesor.
items.en: I explain the problem to the teacher.
items.note: omitting le here sounds wrong in Spanish

items.hr: Siempre les cuento la verdad a mis amigos.
items.en: I always tell my friends the truth.
items.note: les = to them, doubling with 'a mis amigos'

activities.title: La duplicación obligatoria
activities.intro: Practise keeping le or les even when the person is already named.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál de estas frases es natural en español?
options: Le doy el regalo a mi madre.
Doy el regalo a mi madre.
Doy le regalo a mi madre.
A mi madre doy el regalo.
questions.answer: Le doy el regalo a mi madre.
questions.explanation: Spanish keeps the pronoun le even though 'a mi madre' already names the person.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué pronombre corresponde a 'a mis hermanos' en '___ escribo un mensaje a mis hermanos'?
questions.explanation: a mis hermanos is plural, so the indirect object pronoun is les.

questions.prompt: Completa: _____ compro un regalo a mi amiga.
questions.explanation: a mi amiga is singular, so the pronoun is le.

questions.prompt: Completa: La reunión empieza _____ las nueve en punto.
questions.explanation: clock time in Spanish is introduced with a las (plural) or a la (one o'clock).

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I explain the exercise to the students.'
questions.explanation: les doubles 'a los estudiantes', which is plural.

activities.title: Un regalo para mamá
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk about gifts for family, always doubling the indirect object pronoun.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué le compras a tu madre para su cumpleaños?
lines.en: What are you buying your mother for her birthday?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Le compro unas flores y un libro.
lines.en: I'm buying her some flowers and a book.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Le escribes también una tarjeta?
lines.en: Are you also writing her a card?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, siempre le escribo una tarjeta bonita.
lines.en: Yes, I always write her a nice card.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y a tus hermanos? ¿Les compras algo?
lines.en: And your brothers? Are you buying them something?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Les compro chocolate, les gusta mucho.
lines.en: I'm buying them chocolate, they like it a lot.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Qué buena idea. ¿Les cuentas el plan?
lines.en: What a good idea. Are you telling them the plan?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, no les cuento nada todavía, es una sorpresa.
lines.en: No, I'm not telling them anything yet, it's a surprise.

days.title: Se lo doy: los dos pronombres juntos
days.objective: The learner can combine an indirect and a direct object pronoun in the same sentence, correctly turning le or les into se before lo, la, los or las, and can transform full-noun sentences into this double-pronoun form.
days.paretoFocus: This single transformation, saying se lo doy instead of the impossible le lo doy, is the hardest formal point of A2 Spanish and is exactly what marks fluent, natural speech apart from word-for-word translation.
drills: Take five sentences with le doy X and rewrite each one, swapping in the matching direct-object pronoun and changing le to se.
Say aloud: Le doy el libro becomes Se lo doy, five times with different objects until it is automatic.
Write down the rule in your own words: why can le or les never sit directly beside a direct-object pronoun?

items: Recall the redundant doubling rule with le and les.
Recall a sentence with le doy or les mando.
Recall how to replace las llaves with a pronoun.

activities.title: Se lo, se la, se los, se las
activities.intro: Le and les are indirect object pronouns; lo, la, los and las are direct ones. When both sit side by side in a sentence, the indirect pronoun comes first, but Spanish will not let le or les stand right next to one beginning with l-, so it swaps them for se instead, giving se lo doy rather than le lo doy.

items.hr: Le doy el cuaderno a Marta.
items.en: I give the notebook to Marta.
items.note: step one: the indirect object le, as in the previous lesson

items.hr: Se lo doy.
items.en: I give it to her.
items.note: le + lo becomes se lo: le and les can never stand next to lo, la, los or las

items.hr: Les mando la carta. Se la mando.
items.en: I send them the letter. I send it to them.
items.note: les + la also becomes se la, never 'les la'

items.hr: 'Le lo doy' no existe en español.
items.en: 'Le lo doy' does not exist in Spanish.
items.note: a common mistake to avoid: le or les never appear right before lo, la, los or las

items.hr: ¿Le prestas el coche a tu hermano? Sí, se lo presto.
items.en: Do you lend your brother the car? Yes, I lend it to him.
items.note: the order is always indirect then direct: se lo, se la, se los, se las

activities.title: Transforma: le/les + lo/la/los/las
activities.intro: Practise the transformation itself: turn a full sentence with le or les into its double-pronoun form.

questions.prompt: ¿Cómo se dice bien 'I give it to her' hablando de un regalo?
questions.explanation: el regalo is masculine, so lo; le becomes se right before lo.

questions.prompt: Transforma con pronombres dobles: 'Les explico la lección.'
questions.explanation: la lección is feminine, so la; les becomes se right before la.

questions.prompt: Por la mañana le mando los documentos a mi jefe. Transforma la última parte con pronombres dobles: _____ mando.
questions.explanation: los documentos is masculine plural, so los; le becomes se before los.

questions.prompt: Transforma con pronombres dobles: 'Le compro las entradas a mi amigo.' _____ compro.
questions.explanation: las entradas is feminine plural, so las; le becomes se before las.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I lend it to them.' (el coche)
questions.explanation: les becomes se before lo, which stands for el coche.

activities.title: El favor entre amigos
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Lend things to a friend's brother, using se lo, se la and se las throughout.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Le prestas tu coche a tu hermano este fin de semana?
lines.en: Are you lending your brother your car this weekend?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, se lo presto sin problema.
lines.en: Yes, I'm lending it to him, no problem.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y las llaves? ¿Se las das ahora?
lines.en: And the keys? Are you giving them to him now?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, se las doy el viernes por la tarde.
lines.en: No, I'm giving them to him Friday afternoon.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Le explicas cómo funciona el aparcamiento?
lines.en: Are you explaining how the parking works to him?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro, se lo explico todo con calma.
lines.en: Of course, I explain it all to him calmly.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Muy bien. ¿Le mandas la dirección también?
lines.en: Very good. Are you sending him the address too?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, se la mando por mensaje esta noche.
lines.en: Yes, I'm sending it to him by message tonight.

days.title: El lugar de los pronombres
days.objective: The learner can place object and reflexive pronouns correctly before the conjugated verb, or attached to the end of an infinitive or gerund, with both positions valid when a periphrasis is involved.
days.paretoFocus: Getting pronoun position wrong is instantly noticeable to a native ear, and this rule covers almost every sentence built with a modal verb or a gerund.
drills: Rewrite three sentences with tener que + infinitive both ways: pronoun before, and pronoun attached to the infinitive.
Say aloud Lo tengo que hacer and Tengo que hacerlo until both feel equally natural.
Write two sentences with estar + gerundio, attaching the pronoun to the gerund.

items: Recall why le lo doy is impossible in Spanish.
Recall a sentence using se lo or se la.
Recall the reflexive form of acostarse for nosotros.

activities.title: Antes del verbo, o pegado al final
activities.intro: Object and reflexive pronouns usually sit just ahead of a conjugated verb, but Spanish also lets them ride along stuck onto an infinitive or a gerund instead. When a periphrasis such as tener que + infinitive or estar + gerundio is involved, either placement is grammatical and the meaning stays identical.

items.hr: Lo tengo que hacer hoy.
items.en: I have to do it today.
items.note: pronoun before the conjugated verb tengo

items.hr: Tengo que hacerlo hoy.
items.en: I have to do it today.
items.note: same meaning, pronoun attached to the infinitive hacer

items.hr: Me lo estoy pensando.
items.en: I'm thinking it over.
items.note: pronoun before estoy

items.hr: Estoy pensándomelo.
items.en: I'm thinking it over.
items.note: pronoun attached to the gerund; note the written accent that appears

items.hr: ¿Se lo puedes explicar otra vez?
items.en: Can you explain it to him again?
items.note: with a periphrasis, both positions are equally correct

activities.title: Las dos posiciones
activities.intro: Practise both valid pronoun positions with periphrases.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál de estas frases es correcta?
questions.explanation: with ir a + infinitive, the pronoun attaches to the infinitive: comprarlo.

questions.prompt: Elige la opción equivalente a 'Lo tengo que terminar'.
questions.explanation: the pronoun can also attach to the infinitive after tener que, with the same meaning.

questions.prompt: Completa, con el pronombre pegado: Estoy _____ (leer + lo) ahora mismo.
questions.explanation: when the pronoun attaches to the gerund, a written accent appears because the stressed syllable moves.

questions.prompt: Completa: Todos los días _____ (acostarse) a las once.
questions.explanation: acostarse is o>ue, and yo takes me: me acuesto.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I can explain it to you tomorrow.'
questions.explanation: with poder + infinitive, the pronouns can go before the conjugated verb puedo.

activities.title: ¿Cuándo lo haces?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk about a report, showing both valid pronoun positions.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cuándo vas a terminar el informe?
lines.en: When are you going to finish the report?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Lo tengo que terminar mañana, o tengo que terminarlo mañana, las dos son correctas.
lines.en: I have to finish it tomorrow, or I have to finish it tomorrow, both are correct.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Te lo puedo revisar esta noche?
lines.en: Can I check it for you tonight?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro, puedes revisármelo o me lo puedes revisar.
lines.en: Sure, you can check it for me, either way works.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Todavía te lo estás pensando, lo del nuevo trabajo?
lines.en: Are you still thinking it over, the new job thing?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, todavía me lo estoy pensando.
lines.en: Yes, I'm still thinking it over.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Se lo cuentas a tu jefe pronto?
lines.en: Are you going to tell your boss soon?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Se lo voy a contar la semana que viene.
lines.en: I'm going to tell him next week.

days.title: El leísmo
days.objective: The learner can recognise leísmo, using le instead of lo for a male direct object as in Le vi, as an accepted peninsular variant, while continuing to produce lo as the taught form.
days.paretoFocus: Learners will hear le vi constantly in Spain and need to understand it without being taught to produce it, since the course's own written norm is lo.
drills: Listen for le used as a direct object in any Spanish audio and note it down.
Write the same sentence twice: once with lo, the taught form, and once with le, what you'll hear.
Explain in one sentence why leísmo is not a mistake but also not what you should write.

items: Recall both positions where a pronoun can go with tener que.
Recall the written accent that appears on pensándomelo.
Recall a sentence combining se with lo or la.

activities.title: Le por lo, un rasgo peninsular
activities.intro: In much of Spain, le is used instead of lo as a direct object pronoun, but only for a male person, never for a thing. The course teaches lo as the written norm and expects you to recognise le when you hear it.

items.hr: Lo vi ayer en el parque.
items.en: I saw him yesterday in the park.
items.note: lo = the taught direct object form

items.hr: Le vi ayer en el parque.
items.en: I saw him yesterday in the park.
items.note: le for a male person is common in Spain, accepted, not an error

items.hr: Lo vi a él, no a ella.
items.en: I saw him, not her.
items.note: lo stays the recommended written form

items.hr: En España oyes mucho 'le conozco bien'.
items.en: In Spain you hear 'I know him well' a lot.
items.note: leísmo, only with a male person, never with things

items.hr: El lápiz, lo tengo aquí.
items.en: The pencil, I have it here.
items.note: leísmo never applies to things, only to a male person

activities.title: Le o lo
activities.intro: Practise recognising leísmo and keeping lo as your own written form.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué es el leísmo?
options: Usar 'le' en vez de 'lo' para una persona masculina
questions.answer: Usar 'le' en vez de 'lo' para una persona masculina
questions.explanation: leísmo replaces the masculine direct object lo with le, only for people.

questions.prompt: ¿En cuál de estas frases el uso de 'le' NO es aceptable?
questions.explanation: le for a male person is accepted leísmo in Spain, but le for a thing is not accepted; a book takes lo.

questions.prompt: Completa, con la forma enseñada en el curso: A Pablo no _____ veo mucho este año.
questions.explanation: the course's taught written form for a direct object person is lo, not le.

questions.prompt: Completa: Mi madre _____ (llamarse) Carmen.
questions.explanation: llamarse uses a pronoun that marks naming, not a literal reflexive action: se llama.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I know him well, but I don't see him often.'
questions.explanation: the taught form uses lo twice, once for each verb, instead of leísta le.

activities.title: ¿Lo conoces?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend uses leísmo; you stick to the taught form lo.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Conoces a Javier? Le vi ayer en el centro.
lines.en: Do you know Javier? I saw him yesterday downtown.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, lo conozco bien, trabajamos juntos.
lines.en: Yes, I know him well, we work together.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Aquí decimos mucho 'le vi', ¿tú también lo dices?
lines.en: Here we say 'le vi' a lot, do you say it too?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A veces, pero prefiero decir 'lo vi'.
lines.en: Sometimes, but I prefer to say 'lo vi'.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y con las cosas? ¿También dices 'le'?
lines.en: And with things? Do you also say 'le'?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, con las cosas siempre digo 'lo': el coche, lo tengo aquí.
lines.en: No, with things I always say 'lo': the car, I have it here.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tiene sentido, el leísmo es solo con personas.
lines.en: That makes sense, leísmo is only with people.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Exacto, y solo con hombres, no con mujeres.
lines.en: Exactly, and only with men, not with women.

days.title: Repaso: los pronombres en conversación
days.objective: The learner can use direct, indirect and double object pronouns fluently together in a connected conversation, choosing the right form and position without hesitating.
days.paretoFocus: Real conversations mix all these pronoun types in the same breath, so consolidation practice is what turns separate rules into one working system.
drills: Record yourself for one minute answering questions using only pronouns, never repeating the noun.
Write a short dialogue of your own using lo, la, le, se lo and a reflexive verb.
Review your notes from the last five lessons and pick the one pronoun rule you still hesitate on.

items: Recall what lo means in the taught, written form of Spanish.
Recall a sentence with le vi and its meaning.
Recall why leísmo never applies to a thing.

activities.title: Todo junto
activities.intro: This lesson mixes every pronoun type from this block in short, natural exchanges, so the system starts to feel automatic rather than separate rules.

items.hr: ¿Me prestas el diccionario? Sí, te lo presto.
items.en: Will you lend me the dictionary? Yes, I'll lend it to you.
items.note: me becomes te lo in the answer; indirect and direct combine

items.hr: ¿Le diste la noticia a tu madre? Sí, se la di ayer.
items.en: Did you give your mother the news? Yes, I gave it to her yesterday.
items.note: le becomes se before la

items.hr: Estoy explicándoselo a mi jefe.
items.en: I'm explaining it to my boss.
items.note: double pronoun attached to the gerund, with the written accent

items.hr: Nos levantamos y nos lo pensamos con calma.
items.en: We get up and we think it over calmly.
items.note: a reflexive verb and a double pronoun in the same sentence

items.hr: No lo conozco, pero lo voy a conocer pronto.
items.en: I don't know him, but I'm going to meet him soon.
items.note: lo stays lo, never le, in the taught form

activities.title: Repaso general de pronombres
activities.intro: Practise choosing the right pronoun and position across every type from this block.

questions.prompt: Elige la transformación correcta de 'Le doy las gracias a mi profesora'.
questions.explanation: las gracias is feminine plural, so las; le becomes se.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál de estas frases usa el orden correcto de los pronombres?
questions.explanation: the pronoun pair se lo goes together, right before the conjugated verb.

questions.prompt: Completa: ¿Las fotos? _____ mando a mi madre esta noche.
questions.explanation: las fotos is feminine plural, so las; le becomes se before las.

questions.prompt: Completa: Ahora mismo _____ (estar + escribir) un mensaje.
questions.explanation: estar + gerundio for an action happening right now: estoy escribiendo.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I already gave it to them yesterday.'
questions.explanation: les becomes se before lo, and ya opens the sentence.

activities.title: Todo en una conversación
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Mix every pronoun type from this block in one natural exchange.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Me prestas tus apuntes de la clase?
lines.en: Will you lend me your class notes?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro, te los presto esta tarde.
lines.en: Sure, I'll lend them to you this afternoon.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Le diste la noticia a Carla?
lines.en: Did you tell Carla the news?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, se la di anoche por teléfono.
lines.en: Yes, I told her last night on the phone.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y a tus padres? ¿Se lo cuentas hoy?
lines.en: And your parents? Are you telling them today?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Se lo voy a contar este fin de semana.
lines.en: I'm going to tell them this weekend.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Estoy pensándomelo, si les cuento mi plan también.
lines.en: I'm thinking it over, whether I tell them my plan too.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Puedes contárselo, seguro que les gusta.
lines.en: You can tell them, I'm sure they'll like it.

days.title: El pretérito perfecto: he hablado
days.objective: The learner can form the pretérito perfecto with the present of haber plus a regular past participle, to talk about actions connected to now.
days.paretoFocus: The perfecto is the ordinary way Spain talks about today's past, and building it from a present tense already known makes it the easiest new tense to acquire.
drills: Conjugate haber alone: he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han.
Turn five -ar, -er and -ir verbs into their regular participle: hablar, comer, vivir, trabajar, salir.
Say five sentences about today using he plus a participle.

items: Recall the rule for combining le or les with lo, la, los or las.
Recall both correct positions for a pronoun with a periphrasis.
Recall how leísmo differs from the taught written form.

activities.title: Haber más participio
activities.intro: This compound tense pairs a present-tense form of haber (he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han) with a past participle, always in that order. Regular participles end in -ado for -ar verbs and -ido for -er and -ir verbs.

items.hr: He hablado con mi jefe esta mañana.
items.en: I have talked with my boss this morning.
items.note: haber (he) + participle (hablado)

items.hr: ¿Has comido ya?
items.en: Have you eaten yet?
items.note: has = tú form of haber

items.hr: Ha trabajado mucho hoy.
items.en: He/she has worked a lot today.
items.note: ha = él/ella/usted form

items.hr: Hemos vivido aquí dos años.
items.en: We have lived here for two years.
items.note: hemos = nosotros form

items.hr: ¿Habéis salido esta semana?
items.en: Have you all gone out this week?
items.note: habéis = vosotros form, peninsular

activities.title: He, has, ha...
activities.intro: Practise conjugating haber and building regular participles.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma correcta de 'nosotros' de haber?
questions.explanation: the nosotros form of haber is hemos, an irregular present.

questions.prompt: ¿Cómo se forma el participio regular de 'trabajar'?
questions.explanation: -ar verbs form the regular participle with -ado: trabajado.

questions.prompt: Completa: Yo _____ (hablar, perfecto) con ella esta mañana.
questions.explanation: he (haber, yo) + hablado (regular participle of hablar).

questions.prompt: Completa: ¿Y tus llaves? _____ tengo en el bolso.
questions.explanation: las llaves is feminine plural, so the direct object pronoun is las.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'We have lived here two years.'
questions.explanation: hemos (haber, nosotros) + vivido (regular participle of vivir).

activities.title: ¿Qué has hecho hoy?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk about today using the pretérito perfecto.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué has hecho hoy?
lines.en: What have you done today?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: He trabajado toda la mañana.
lines.en: I've worked all morning.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Has comido algo?
lines.en: Have you eaten anything?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, he comido un bocadillo rápido.
lines.en: Yes, I've eaten a quick sandwich.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Habéis salido tu compañero y tú esta semana?
lines.en: Have you and your colleague gone out this week?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, hemos trabajado mucho, no hemos salido.
lines.en: No, we've worked a lot, we haven't gone out.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Ha llamado tu jefe otra vez?
lines.en: Has your boss called again?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, ha llamado dos veces esta tarde.
lines.en: Yes, he's called twice this afternoon.

days.title: Participios irregulares
days.objective: The learner can recognise and correctly use the eight common irregular participles (hecho, escrito, visto, puesto, dicho, vuelto, abierto, roto) in the pretérito perfecto.
days.paretoFocus: These eight verbs are among the most frequent in the language, so their irregular participles have to be automatic rather than calculated each time.
drills: Memorise the list in pairs: hacer/hecho, escribir/escrito, ver/visto, poner/puesto, decir/dicho, volver/vuelto, abrir/abierto, romper/roto.
Write one perfecto sentence for each of the eight verbs.
Quiz yourself: say the infinitive, answer with the participle, for all eight.

items: Recall the present tense of haber alone.
Recall a sentence with a direct object pronoun replacing a noun.
Recall the gerund of dormir.

activities.title: Los ocho participios irregulares
activities.intro: A small group of very frequent verbs have an irregular participle that must be memorised, since none of them follow the regular -ado/-ido pattern.

items.hr: He hecho la cena.
items.en: I have made dinner.
items.note: hacer -> hecho

items.hr: ¿Has escrito el correo?
items.en: Have you written the email?
items.note: escribir -> escrito

items.hr: Hemos visto esa película dos veces.
items.en: We have seen that film twice.
items.note: ver -> visto

items.hr: He puesto la mesa y he abierto la ventana.
items.en: I have set the table and opened the window.
items.note: poner -> puesto; abrir -> abierto

items.hr: Ha dicho la verdad, pero ha vuelto tarde y ha roto un plato.
items.en: He has told the truth, but he has come back late and broken a plate.
items.note: decir -> dicho; volver -> vuelto; romper -> roto

activities.title: Ocho participios que hay que saber
activities.intro: Practise the eight irregular participles.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es el participio de 'escribir'?
questions.explanation: escribir has the irregular participle escrito.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es el participio de 'romper'?
questions.explanation: romper has the irregular participle roto.

questions.prompt: Completa: Todavía no _____ (hacer) los deberes.
questions.explanation: hacer has the irregular participle hecho: he hecho.

questions.prompt: Completa: A mis padres _____ mando un mensaje cada domingo.
questions.explanation: a mis padres is plural, so the indirect object pronoun is les.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'She has opened all the windows.'
questions.explanation: abrir has the irregular participle abierto.

activities.title: La casa después de la fiesta
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Describe the mess after a party using irregular participles.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Has visto la cocina? Está fatal.
lines.en: Have you seen the kitchen? It's a mess.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, alguien ha roto un vaso.
lines.en: Yes, someone has broken a glass.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Quién ha puesto la música tan alta?
lines.en: Who has put the music so loud?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ha sido Marcos, él lo ha dicho.
lines.en: It was Marcos, he said so himself.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Has abierto las ventanas de la cocina?
lines.en: Have you opened the kitchen windows?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, y ya he puesto un poco de orden.
lines.en: Yes, and I've already tidied up a bit.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Ha vuelto Marcos a ayudar?
lines.en: Has Marcos come back to help?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, todavía no ha vuelto.
lines.en: No, he hasn't come back yet.

days.title: Los marcadores del pretérito perfecto
days.objective: The learner can recognise the time markers hoy, esta mañana, esta semana, este año, ya, todavía no, alguna vez and nunca that signal the perfecto in peninsular Spanish, and knows that most of America expresses the same idea with the indefinido.
days.paretoFocus: Choosing the right past tense in Spain depends almost entirely on recognising these markers, and knowing the American difference prevents confusion when the learner hears or reads American Spanish.
drills: List all eight peninsular perfecto markers from memory, in any order you like.
Write three sentences with hoy or esta semana and the perfecto.
Explain out loud what a speaker from Mexico would likely say instead of hoy he comido.

items: Recall the participle of hacer and of escribir.
Recall a sentence with se lo or se la.
Recall the position of a pronoun attached to an infinitive.

activities.title: Marcadores de hoy
activities.intro: The perfecto pairs with time expressions that still reach into the present moment, anchored to today, this week or this year, rather than a period sealed off in the past. Words like ya and todavía no work the same way, framing something as relevant right now.

items.hr: Hoy he comido en un restaurante nuevo.
items.en: Today I have eaten at a new restaurant.
items.note: hoy = a period that still includes now

items.hr: Esta semana hemos trabajado mucho.
items.en: This week we have worked a lot.
items.note: esta semana still includes today

items.hr: Todavía no he terminado el informe.
items.en: I haven't finished the report yet.
items.note: todavía no = negative marker for the perfecto

items.hr: ¿Has estado alguna vez en Sevilla?
items.en: Have you ever been to Sevilla?
items.note: alguna vez asks about experience, with no specific time

items.hr: En España decimos 'hoy he comido'; en gran parte de América dicen 'hoy comí'.
items.en: In Spain we say 'hoy he comido'; in much of America they say 'hoy comí'.
items.note: a variety difference, not an error: America favours the indefinido here

activities.title: ¿Qué marcador es?
activities.intro: Sort each time clue into the one that calls for the perfecto and the one that does not.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué marcador NO suele pedir el pretérito perfecto en España?
questions.explanation: el año pasado names a closed past period, so it takes the indefinido, not the perfecto.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué dice un hablante mexicano en vez de 'Hoy he comido'?
questions.explanation: much of America uses the indefinido, comí, for the same idea Spain expresses with he comido.

questions.prompt: Completa: _____ no he leído ese libro.
questions.explanation: todavía no marks something not yet done.

questions.prompt: Completa: Se lo _____ explicar mañana, si quieres.
questions.explanation: poder + infinitive, with the pronoun pair se lo already in front of the conjugated verb.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'This year we have traveled a lot.'
questions.explanation: este año is a marker for the perfecto, since it still includes the present.

activities.title: Marcadores de hoy
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Use the perfecto markers, and note the American contrast.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Has estado alguna vez en Portugal?
lines.en: Have you ever been to Portugal?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, he estado dos veces, la última este año.
lines.en: Yes, I've been twice, the last time this year.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué has hecho esta semana?
lines.en: What have you done this week?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: He tenido mucho trabajo, todavía no he descansado.
lines.en: I've had a lot of work, I haven't rested yet.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: En mi país decimos 'hoy trabajé', no 'he trabajado'.
lines.en: In my country we say 'hoy trabajé', not 'he trabajado'.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Aquí en España usamos más el perfecto para hoy.
lines.en: Here in Spain we use the perfecto more for today.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Ya has comido algo hoy?
lines.en: Have you eaten anything today yet?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, todavía no he comido nada.
lines.en: No, I haven't eaten anything yet.

days.title: Hablar de experiencias
days.objective: The learner can ask about and describe life experience using ¿Has + participio alguna vez...? and Nunca he + participio, without yet contrasting this with the indefinido.
days.paretoFocus: Asking what somebody has done opens more real conversations than any grammar point at this level, and the pattern transfers unchanged to every other verb.
drills: Ask three people you know ¿Has probado...? about a food, a place and an activity.
Write two sentences starting Nunca he... about things you truly have never done.
Answer ¿Has estado alguna vez en...? about three cities.

items: Recall three markers that call for the perfecto.
Recall an irregular participle from the last lesson.
Recall how pronouns combine before a conjugated verb.

activities.title: ¿Has probado...? Nunca he...
activities.intro: Alguna vez asks whether something has ever happened; nunca states it never has. Both combine with the perfecto in a fixed, reusable pattern.

items.hr: ¿Has probado el gazpacho alguna vez?
items.en: Have you ever tried gazpacho?
items.note: ¿Has + participio alguna vez...?

items.hr: Nunca he probado el pulpo.
items.en: I have never tried octopus.
items.note: nunca + he + participio

items.hr: ¿Habéis visitado el museo alguna vez?
items.en: Have you all ever visited the museum?
items.note: vosotros form of the same pattern

items.hr: He viajado a muchos países, pero nunca he estado en Asia.
items.en: I have traveled to many countries, but I have never been to Asia.
items.note: a contrast within the perfecto itself

items.hr: ¿Ha vivido tu abuela alguna vez fuera de España?
items.en: Has your grandmother ever lived outside Spain?
items.note: third person, same fixed pattern

activities.title: Alguna vez, nunca
activities.intro: Practise asking about and describing experience.

questions.prompt: ¿Cómo se pregunta por una experiencia en la vida?
questions.explanation: alguna vez with the perfecto asks about life experience, with no specific date.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma correcta de decir 'I have never tried it'?
questions.explanation: nunca combines with the perfecto, he probado, for this pattern.

questions.prompt: Completa: ¿_____ probado alguna vez la paella?
questions.explanation: the tú form of haber, has, opens this question about experience.

questions.prompt: Completa: El coche, _____ presto a mi hermano si lo necesita.
questions.explanation: le becomes se before lo, which stands for el coche.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I have never lived abroad.'
questions.explanation: nunca + he + vivido is the fixed experience pattern.

activities.title: ¿Lo has probado alguna vez?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk about food, travel and family experience.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Has probado el gazpacho alguna vez?
lines.en: Have you ever tried gazpacho?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, lo he probado muchas veces, me gusta mucho.
lines.en: Yes, I've tried it many times, I like it a lot.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y el pulpo a la gallega?
lines.en: And Galician-style octopus?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Nunca lo he probado, la verdad.
lines.en: I've never tried it, honestly.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Habéis viajado tú y tu familia fuera de Europa?
lines.en: Have you and your family traveled outside Europe?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Hemos viajado a Marruecos una vez.
lines.en: We've traveled to Morocco once.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Ha vivido alguien de tu familia en otro país?
lines.en: Has anyone in your family lived in another country?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, mi hermana ha vivido dos años en Alemania.
lines.en: Yes, my sister has lived in Germany for two years.

days.title: Ya y todavía no
days.objective: The learner can use ya (already, or yet in questions) and todavía no (not yet) correctly with the pretérito perfecto to say whether something has happened.
days.paretoFocus: These two small words carry enormous conversational weight, confirming or denying whether something is done, and English speakers routinely misplace or omit them.
drills: Write three questions with ¿Ya has...? about daily tasks.
Answer each with either Sí, ya he... or No, todavía no he....
Notice the position: ya usually comes right before he/has/ha; todavía no usually comes right before too.

items: Recall how to ask about a past experience with alguna vez.
Recall a sentence with nunca and the perfecto.
Recall the marker todavía no in a full sentence.

activities.title: Ya, todavía no
activities.intro: Ya asks or confirms that something is already done; todavía no denies it so far. Both usually sit right before the form of haber.

items.hr: ¿Ya has cenado?
items.en: Have you already eaten dinner?
items.note: ya before the auxiliary, asking if something is done

items.hr: Sí, ya he cenado.
items.en: Yes, I've already eaten dinner.
items.note: confirms completion

items.hr: No, todavía no he cenado.
items.en: No, I haven't eaten dinner yet.
items.note: todavía no denies completion so far

items.hr: ¿Ya habéis decidido el plan?
items.en: Have you all decided on the plan yet?
items.note: vosotros form

items.hr: Ya lo he hecho, no te preocupes.
items.en: I've already done it, don't worry.
items.note: ya with a direct object pronoun review

activities.title: ¿Ya o todavía no?
activities.intro: Practise confirming or denying completion with ya and todavía no.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la respuesta correcta a '¿Ya has llamado a tu madre?' si NO lo has hecho?
options: No, todavía no la he llamado.
questions.answer: No, todavía no la he llamado.
questions.explanation: todavía no denies completion so far, matching a 'not yet' answer.

questions.prompt: ¿Dónde suele ir 'ya' en la frase?
options: Al final de la frase siempre
questions.explanation: ya usually sits right before the conjugated form of haber.

questions.prompt: Completa: _____ he terminado el examen.
questions.explanation: ya confirms that something is already done.

questions.prompt: Completa: ¿Y esa cena? _____ estoy preparando ahora.
questions.explanation: la cena is feminine singular, so the direct object pronoun is la.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'We haven't decided yet.'
questions.explanation: todavía no denies completion, right before hemos decidido.

activities.title: ¿Ya lo has hecho?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Confirm and deny whether tasks are already done.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Ya has hecho la compra?
lines.en: Have you already done the shopping?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, ya la he hecho esta mañana.
lines.en: Yes, I've already done it this morning.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y has llamado al médico?
lines.en: And have you called the doctor?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, todavía no lo he llamado.
lines.en: No, I haven't called him yet.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Ya habéis decidido dónde ir de vacaciones?
lines.en: Have you all already decided where to go on vacation?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Todavía no lo hemos decidido.
lines.en: We haven't decided yet.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Ya te has puesto de acuerdo con tu hermana sobre la fecha?
lines.en: Have you already agreed with your sister on the date?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, ya nos hemos puesto de acuerdo.
lines.en: Yes, we've already agreed.

days.title: Repaso: lo que has hecho hoy
days.objective: The learner can narrate a connected account of the day's activities using the perfecto, regular and irregular participles, and the markers from this block, without translating word by word.
days.paretoFocus: Consolidation turns isolated forms into the ability to actually answer 'what have you done today', the single most common real use of this tense.
drills: Narrate your real day so far out loud using at least six perfecto verbs.
Write eight sentences: four with regular participles, four with irregular ones.
Ask a friend ¿Qué has hecho hoy? and answer using ya and todavía no.

items: Recall where ya usually goes in a perfecto sentence.
Recall a reflexive verb used in the perfecto.
Recall the meaning of se lo in a sentence you've already used.

activities.title: El día contado
activities.intro: This review lesson knits the whole block together: reflexive verbs, participles both regular and irregular, plus the markers ya and todavía no, all woven into one continuous account of a single day.

items.hr: Hoy me he levantado temprano y he desayunado rápido.
items.en: Today I got up early and had a quick breakfast.
items.note: reflexive perfecto: me he levantado

items.hr: He escrito dos correos y he hecho una llamada importante.
items.en: I have written two emails and made an important call.
items.note: regular and irregular participle together

items.hr: Todavía no he comido, pero ya he terminado el trabajo de hoy.
items.en: I haven't eaten yet, but I've already finished today's work.
items.note: contrast within the same sentence

items.hr: ¿Qué has hecho tú esta mañana?
items.en: What have you done this morning?
items.note: the question that opens the whole block

items.hr: Nunca he tenido un día tan ocupado como hoy.
items.en: I've never had such a busy day as today.
items.note: nunca + experience, applied to today

activities.title: Un día entero en perfecto
activities.intro: Practise narrating a whole day using the perfecto.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál de estas frases significa 'I have done a thousand things today, I haven't stopped'?
options: He hecho mil cosas hoy, no he parado.
questions.answer: He hecho mil cosas hoy, no he parado.
questions.explanation: only the yo form, he hecho, matches a first-person account of the speaker's own day.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué forma es correcta para 'we have gotten up early'?
questions.explanation: the reflexive pronoun nos goes before hemos, and the participle levantado stays invariable.

questions.prompt: Completa: Hoy _____ (escribir) tres correos.
questions.explanation: escribir has the irregular participle escrito: he escrito.

questions.prompt: Completa: A Marcos no _____ veo mucho este mes.
questions.explanation: the course's taught written form for a direct object person is lo, not le.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I have never had such a busy day.'
questions.explanation: nunca + he tenido states this has never happened, and tan ocupado describes the day.

activities.title: Un resumen del día
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Narrate a busy day using everything from this block.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué has hecho hoy? Quiero saberlo todo.
lines.en: What have you done today? I want to know everything.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: He hecho muchísimas cosas, no he parado.
lines.en: I've done so many things, I haven't stopped.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Ya has comido algo?
lines.en: Have you eaten anything yet?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, aún no he comido nada, he estado muy liado.
lines.en: No, I still haven't eaten anything, I've been really busy.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Has escrito ya el informe?
lines.en: Have you written the report yet?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, lo he escrito y se lo he mandado a mi jefe.
lines.en: Yes, I've written it and sent it to my boss.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vaya día. ¿Te has levantado muy temprano?
lines.en: What a day. Did you get up very early?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, me he levantado a las seis, nunca he tenido un día tan largo.
lines.en: Yes, I got up at six, I've never had such a long day.

days.title: El pretérito indefinido: formas regulares
days.objective: The learner can conjugate regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs in the pretérito indefinido, placing the written accent correctly on the yo and él/ella/usted forms.
days.paretoFocus: The indefinido is the tense for a finished, dated past action, and its whole difficulty lives in the accent, hablé versus hablo versus habla, so getting the accent right is the entire task.
drills: Write out the full indefinido of hablar, comer and vivir, marking every accent by hand.
Say aloud hablé/habló, comí/comió, viví/vivió, five times each until the stress feels automatic.
Circle the two accented forms in each conjugation: él/ella/usted first, then yo.

items: Recall three markers that trigger the perfecto rather than the indefinido.
Recall an irregular participle you learned this block.
Recall a full sentence you can say about today using the perfecto.

activities.title: Hablé, comí, viví
activities.intro: The pretérito indefinido narrates a completed action anchored to one specific moment in the past. Two of the six regular endings, él/ella/usted and yo, carry a written accent, and dropping that accent mark changes which verb form you mean.

items.hr: Ayer hablé con mi madre por teléfono.
items.en: Yesterday I talked with my mother on the phone.
items.note: hablé carries the accent; without it, 'hable' is a different form

items.hr: Ella habló despacio y con claridad.
items.en: She spoke slowly and clearly.
items.note: habló, third person, also accented

items.hr: Comí en casa de mis abuelos el domingo.
items.en: I ate at my grandparents' house on Sunday.
items.note: comí, -er verb, accented yo form

items.hr: ¿Comió Juan con vosotros?
items.en: Did Juan eat with you all?
items.note: comió, third person, also accented

items.hr: Viví en Bilbao durante dos años.
items.en: I lived in Bilbao for two years.
items.note: viví: -er and -ir verbs share the same indefinido endings

activities.title: El acento que lo cambia todo
activities.intro: Practise the regular indefinido, paying close attention to the written accent.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma correcta de 'yo' de hablar en indefinido?
questions.explanation: the accent on the final e marks the indefinido yo form, hablé, not the él form habló or the present hablo.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué forma lleva tilde: 'hablo' (ahora) o 'habló' (ayer)?
questions.explanation: the él/ella/usted indefinido ending carries a written accent: habló.

questions.prompt: Completa con el acento correcto: Ayer yo _____ (comer) en un restaurante nuevo.
questions.explanation: the yo form of the indefinido for -er verbs is -í, with a written accent: comí.

questions.prompt: Completa con el acento correcto: Ayer por la mañana, yo _____ (hablar) con mi jefe.
questions.explanation: the yo form of the indefinido for -ar verbs is -é, with a written accent: hablé.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Yesterday I lived a very strange day.'
questions.explanation: viví is the accented yo form of vivir in the indefinido.

activities.title: Ayer hablé con ella
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk about yesterday using the regular indefinido.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Hablaste con Marta ayer?
lines.en: Did you talk with Marta yesterday?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, hablé con ella por la tarde.
lines.en: Yes, I talked with her in the afternoon.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y ella habló contigo del trabajo nuevo?
lines.en: And did she talk to you about the new job?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, habló mucho, está muy contenta.
lines.en: Yes, she talked a lot, she's very happy.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Dónde comisteis el domingo pasado?
lines.en: Where did you all eat last Sunday?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Comimos en casa de mis abuelos.
lines.en: We ate at my grandparents' house.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cuánto tiempo viviste en Bilbao?
lines.en: How long did you live in Bilbao?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Viví allí dos años, me gustó mucho la ciudad.
lines.en: I lived there two years, I liked the city a lot.

days.title: Ser e ir, ver y dar
days.objective: The learner can recognise that ser and ir share an identical indefinido conjugation (fui, fuiste, fue...), distinguished only by context, and can conjugate the short irregular forms of ver and dar.
days.paretoFocus: Fui does the work of two entirely unrelated verbs, so a learner has to resolve which one from context every single time it appears, and it appears constantly.
drills: Write five sentences with fui, some meaning 'I was' and some meaning 'I went', and mark which is which.
Conjugate ver and dar fully in the indefinido: vi, viste, vio... di, diste, dio...
Say 'Fui a Madrid' and 'Fui profesor' aloud and notice nothing in the verb itself tells them apart.

items: Recall why hablé carries a written accent and habla does not.
Recall the yo and él forms of comer in the indefinido.
Recall a sentence with vivió or comió.

activities.title: Fui, fuiste, fue...
activities.intro: Ser and ir are identical in the indefinido: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron. Only the rest of the sentence tells you which verb is meant. Ver and dar are also short and irregular, with no accent.

items.hr: Fui a Madrid el verano pasado.
items.en: I went to Madrid last summer.
items.note: fui = ir here, because of 'a Madrid'

items.hr: Fui profesor durante diez años.
items.en: I was a teacher for ten years.
items.note: fui = ser here, because of the noun profesor

items.hr: Fuimos al cine el sábado.
items.en: We went to the cinema on Saturday.
items.note: fuimos, plural, from ir

items.hr: Vi una película muy buena.
items.en: I saw a very good film.
items.note: ver: vi, no accent, a short one-syllable ending

items.hr: Le di un regalo a mi amiga.
items.en: I gave my friend a gift.
items.note: dar: di, also no accent, the same short pattern as vi

activities.title: ¿Ser o ir? ¿Ver o dar?
activities.intro: Practise telling ser and ir apart by context, and using ver and dar.

questions.prompt: En '¿Fuiste a la fiesta?', ¿de qué verbo viene 'fuiste'?
questions.explanation: a la fiesta signals movement, so this fuiste comes from ir.

questions.prompt: En 'Fue una profesora excelente', ¿de qué verbo viene 'fue'?
questions.explanation: una profesora excelente is a description, so this fue comes from ser.

questions.prompt: Completa: Ayer _____ (ver) a mi prima en el mercado.
questions.explanation: ver has the short irregular indefinido form vi, with no accent.

questions.prompt: Completa: ¿El regalo? _____ di a mi madre ayer.
questions.explanation: le becomes se before lo, which stands for el regalo.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I went to Sevilla, and later I was a guide there.'
questions.explanation: the first fui comes from ir (a Sevilla), the second from ser (guía).

activities.title: Fui a Madrid
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Use fui for both ser and ir, and vi and di from ver and dar.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Fuiste a Madrid el mes pasado?
lines.en: Did you go to Madrid last month?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, fui tres días con mi familia.
lines.en: Yes, I went for three days with my family.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Fue tu padre guía turístico alguna vez?
lines.en: Was your father ever a tour guide?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, fue guía durante muchos años.
lines.en: Yes, he was a guide for many years.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Visteis algo interesante en el museo?
lines.en: Did you see anything interesting at the museum?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vimos un cuadro enorme, muy famoso.
lines.en: We saw a huge, very famous painting.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Le diste las gracias al guía?
lines.en: Did you thank the guide?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, le di las gracias y también le di una propina.
lines.en: Yes, I thanked him and also gave him a tip.

days.title: Los pretéritos fuertes
days.objective: The learner can conjugate the strong-stem indefinido verbs tener, estar, hacer, poder and poner, whose endings carry no written accent at all, unlike the regular forms from the previous lesson.
days.paretoFocus: These five verbs are used constantly to narrate anything that happened, and their accent-free endings are a completely different pattern that must not be confused with the regular tense just learned.
drills: Write tuve, estuve, hice, pude, puse and say each aloud, noting that none of them carries a written accent.
Compare hablé (with accent) and tuve (without accent) side by side and say why they differ.
Conjugate tener fully: tuve, tuviste, tuvo, tuvimos, tuvisteis, tuvieron.

items: Recall the two meanings fui can have and how context decides.
Recall the indefinido of ver and dar.
Recall a full sentence with fui a or fui + a profession.

activities.title: Tuve, estuve, hice, pude, puse
activities.intro: A group of very frequent verbs has a strong, irregular stem in the indefinido, and their endings never carry a written accent, unlike the regular hablé or comí.

items.hr: Tuve un problema con el coche ayer.
items.en: I had a problem with the car yesterday.
items.note: tuve, no written accent, unlike hablé

items.hr: Estuve en el hospital toda la tarde.
items.en: I was at the hospital all afternoon.
items.note: estuve follows the same strong pattern as tuve

items.hr: Hice la comida y luego hice la compra.
items.en: I made lunch and then did the shopping.
items.note: hice, strong stem, no accent

items.hr: No pude terminar el trabajo a tiempo.
items.en: I couldn't finish the work on time.
items.note: pude, strong stem

items.hr: Puse la mesa antes de la cena.
items.en: I set the table before dinner.
items.note: puse, strong stem; compare with the accented hablé and comí from the previous lesson

activities.title: Sin acento: los fuertes
activities.intro: Practise the strong-stem indefinido forms, which never carry a written accent.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál de estas formas NO lleva tilde?
questions.explanation: strong-stem indefinido forms like tuve carry no written accent at all.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma correcta de 'yo' de poder en indefinido?
questions.explanation: poder has the strong stem pud- in the indefinido, with the unaccented ending -e: pude.

questions.prompt: Completa: Ayer yo _____ (tener) mucho trabajo.
questions.explanation: tener has the strong stem tuv- in the indefinido, and the yo ending carries no accent: tuve.

questions.prompt: Completa, con el verbo en pretérito perfecto, no en indefinido: Todavía no _____ (hablar) con ella hoy.
questions.explanation: hoy still includes the present, so the perfecto, he hablado, is the taught form here, not hablé.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I had a problem and I couldn't sleep.'
questions.explanation: tuve (tener) and pude (poder) are both strong-stem forms with no written accent.

activities.title: Un día con problemas
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Narrate a difficult day using the strong-stem indefinido.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué tal ayer? Tuviste mala cara por la mañana.
lines.en: How was yesterday? You looked unwell in the morning.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tuve un problema con el coche y estuve una hora esperando.
lines.en: I had a problem with the car and I was waiting for an hour.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¡Vaya! ¿Al final pudiste llegar al trabajo?
lines.en: Wow! Did you manage to get to work in the end?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, pude llegar, pero muy tarde.
lines.en: Yes, I managed to get there, but very late.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Hiciste algo especial por la tarde?
lines.en: Did you do anything special in the afternoon?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Hice la comida y puse la mesa para toda la familia.
lines.en: I made lunch and set the table for the whole family.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Menos mal que el día terminó bien.
lines.en: Good thing the day ended well.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, al final todo salió bien.
lines.en: Yes, in the end everything turned out fine.

days.title: Los pretéritos fuertes (y dos)
days.objective: The learner can conjugate venir, decir, traer, querer, saber and andar in the pretérito indefinido, including the -jeron ending that drops the i.
days.paretoFocus: These six verbs appear constantly in past narration and their strong stems have to be memorised as a group before the tense feels automatic.
drills: Write out the full six-form conjugation of decir and traer from memory.
Say three true sentences about yesterday using vine, dije and supe.
Translate: 'They didn't want to come, so we walked around the city alone.'

items: Recite the strong stems from lesson 64: tener, estar, hacer, poder, poner.
What do the endings for the -jeron group look like, and which two verbs here take them?
What does 'no quise' mean that is different from a simple 'I didn't want to'?

activities.title: Vine, dije, traje…
activities.intro: Six more verbs share the same irregular pattern as tener and estar: a changed stem plus a shared set of endings, with one small twist for two of them.

items.hr: Vine a las nueve porque perdí el autobús.
items.en: I came at nine because I missed the bus.
items.note: venir: vine, viniste, vino, vinimos, vinisteis, vinieron

items.hr: Me dijo la verdad enseguida.
items.en: He told me the truth right away.
items.note: decir: dije, dijiste, dijo, dijimos, dijisteis, dijeron

items.hr: Trajeron sus propias sillas a la terraza.
items.en: They brought their own chairs to the terrace.
items.note: traer: traje…trajeron. The -jeron group drops the i: dijeron and trajeron, never dijieron or trajieron.

items.hr: No quise molestarte con otra llamada.
items.en: I didn't mean to bother you with another call.
items.note: querer: quise, quisiste, quiso, quisimos, quisisteis, quisieron. 'No quise' in the indefinido often means 'I refused', not just 'I didn't feel like it'.

items.hr: Por fin supimos la verdad y anduvimos horas buscando la casa.
items.en: We finally found out the truth and we walked around for hours looking for the house.
items.note: saber: supe…supieron ('supe' = 'I found out'); andar: anduve, anduviste, anduvo, anduvimos, anduvisteis, anduvieron

activities.title: Seis verbos fuertes más
activities.intro: Drill the changed stems of these six verbs, plus the -jeron twist for two of them.

questions.prompt: ¿Cómo se dice 'they said' en el pretérito indefinido?
questions.explanation: The -jeron group drops the i of the ending: dijeron, never dijieron.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma correcta de 'we walked around' (pretérito indefinido de andar)?
questions.explanation: Andar is a strong-stem verb: anduve, anduviste, anduvo, anduvimos, anduvisteis, anduvieron. 'Andamos' is the present tense of the same verb, and 'anduvisteis'/'anduvieron' are the wrong person.

questions.prompt: Completa: Se lo ___ ayer por la tarde. (decir, yo)
questions.explanation: Decir: dije, dijiste, dijo, dijimos, dijisteis, dijeron; 'se lo' keeps the pronoun combination from earlier lessons in front of the verb.

questions.prompt: Completa: ¿Qué ___ (traer, tú) a la fiesta al final?
questions.explanation: Traer: traje, trajiste, trajo, trajimos, trajisteis, trajeron.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'We didn't want to come this year.'
questions.explanation: Querer in the indefinido: no quisimos venir, followed by the time expression este año.

activities.title: ¿A qué hora viniste?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend asks about last night, exercising vine, dijo, trajiste and anduvisteis.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿A qué hora viniste anoche?
lines.en: What time did you come last night?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vine sobre las once, perdí el último autobús.
lines.en: I came around eleven, I missed the last bus.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y qué te dijo tu hermana?
lines.en: And what did your sister tell you?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Me dijo que no pasa nada, que no se enfadó.
lines.en: She told me it's fine, that she didn't get upset.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Trajiste el regalo al final?
lines.en: Did you bring the present in the end?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, lo traje, pero casi lo olvido.
lines.en: Yes, I brought it, but I almost forgot it.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Anduvisteis mucho buscando aparcamiento?
lines.en: Did you two walk around a lot looking for parking?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Uf, anduvimos como media hora dando vueltas.
lines.en: Ugh, we walked around for about half an hour.

days.title: Cambios ortográficos y vocálicos
days.objective: The learner can produce the spelling changes in -car, -gar and -zar verbs and the vowel changes of verbs like leer, dormir and pedir in the pretérito indefinido.
days.paretoFocus: These changes affect extremely common verbs (search, arrive, start, read, sleep, ask) and follow small, predictable rules once seen together.
drills: Write the yo form of buscar, llegar and empezar in the pretérito.
Conjugate leer, dormir and pedir for él/ella and for ellos/ellas, watching the vowel shift.
Translate: 'The waiter asked me for the menu and I looked for my glasses.'

items: What are the four irregular yo-form present verbs from lesson 35?
How is the direct object pronoun 'lo' used in a sentence like 'lo busqué'?
Recall one strong stem from lesson 64 or 65.

activities.title: Busqué, llegué, leyó…
