activities.intro: Two small groups of change appear in the pretérito: a spelling swap that only touches the yo form of verbs ending -car, -gar or -zar, and a vowel swap in the third person of some -er and -ir verbs.

items.hr: Busqué las llaves por toda la casa.
items.en: I looked for the keys all over the house.
items.note: buscar -> busqué (c becomes qu before e, only in the yo form)

items.hr: Llegué tarde a la reunión.
items.en: I arrived late to the meeting.
items.note: llegar -> llegué (g becomes gu before e)

items.hr: Empecé a trabajar a las ocho.
items.en: I started working at eight.
items.note: empezar -> empecé (z becomes c before e)

items.hr: Ella leyó el periódico y luego se durmió.
items.en: She read the newspaper and then fell asleep.
items.note: leer -> leyó, leyeron (unstressed i between vowels becomes y); dormir -> durmió, durmieron (o becomes u only in the third persons)

items.hr: El camarero nos pidió el carné.
items.en: The waiter asked us for our ID.
items.note: pedir -> pidió, pidieron (e becomes i only in the third persons, like servir, seguir and repetir)

activities.title: Ortografía y vocales en el pasado
activities.intro: Practise the yo-form spelling changes and the third-person vowel changes.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma correcta de 'I arrived' (llegar, pretérito indefinido)?
questions.explanation: G becomes gu before e to keep the hard g sound: llegué; 'llegue' without the accent is a different verb form, not the past you want here.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma correcta de la tercera persona de 'dormir' en pretérito?
questions.explanation: Dormir changes o to u only in the third persons (durmió, durmieron); elsewhere the stem is regular.

questions.prompt: Completa: Ayer (yo) ___ una mesa para dos en el restaurante. (buscar)
questions.explanation: Buscar: c becomes qu before e in the yo form: busqué.

questions.prompt: Completa: Los niños ___ toda la noche después del viaje. (dormir, pretérito, ellos)
questions.explanation: Dormir: durmió, durmieron in the third persons.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'The waiter asked me for the menu.'
questions.explanation: Pedir changes e to i in the third person: pidió; 'me' is the indirect object pronoun placed before the verb.

activities.title: ¿Dónde compraste el pan?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend asks about errands and dinner, exercising busqué, llegué, pidió and durmieron.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Dónde compraste el pan?
lines.en: Where did you buy the bread?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Lo busqué en dos tiendas y al final lo encontré en la panadería de la esquina.
lines.en: I looked for it in two shops and finally found it at the corner bakery.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿A qué hora llegaste a casa?
lines.en: What time did you get home?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Llegué sobre la medianoche, el tren se retrasó.
lines.en: I arrived around midnight, the train was delayed.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué pidió tu amigo en el restaurante?
lines.en: What did your friend order at the restaurant?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Pidió pescado, pero yo pedí carne.
lines.en: He ordered fish, but I ordered meat.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y cómo durmieron tus amigos después de la cena?
lines.en: And how did your friends sleep after dinner?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Durmieron fatal, todos comimos demasiado.
lines.en: They slept terribly, we all ate too much.

days.title: Marcadores del pasado: ayer, anoche, hace…
days.objective: The learner can use the standard time markers that trigger the pretérito indefinido to narrate finished past events.
days.paretoFocus: Markers are the most reliable signal for choosing the right past tense and appear in almost every narration task.
drills: List five time markers that always call for the pretérito indefinido.
Write three sentences about last year using el año pasado, hace and en plus a year.
Translate: 'Two years ago I started studying Spanish, and in 2019 I travelled to Madrid.'

items: What do 'hoy' and 'todavía no' have in common that 'ayer' does not share?
Recall the pronoun placement rule from lesson 53 for an infinitive plus a pronoun.
Give the pretérito indefinido of ver in the yo form.

activities.title: Ayer, anoche, hace dos años…
activities.intro: A handful of expressions reliably name a closed period of past time, so whenever one of them appears, the verb goes into the pretérito indefinido.

items.hr: Ayer trabajé desde casa.
items.en: Yesterday I worked from home.
items.note: ayer = yesterday, always indefinido

items.hr: Anoche no dormí bien.
items.en: Last night I didn't sleep well.
items.note: anoche = last night

items.hr: El año pasado viví en Sevilla.
items.en: Last year I lived in Sevilla.
items.note: el año pasado = last year

items.hr: Hace dos años empecé a estudiar español.
items.en: Two years ago I started studying Spanish.
items.note: hace + [time] = ... ago, a closed period

items.hr: En 2019 nació mi sobrina.
items.en: In 2019 my niece was born.
items.note: en + [year] names a closed point in time

activities.title: Cuándo pasó: los marcadores
activities.intro: Practise choosing and using the markers that call for the pretérito indefinido.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué marcador de tiempo pide el pretérito indefinido?
questions.explanation: Ayer names a day that is already over, unlike hoy, todavía no and este año, which can still reach into the present.

questions.prompt: ¿Cómo se dice 'two years ago' en español?
questions.explanation: 'Hace' plus a period of time means 'ago' and always precedes the amount of time.

questions.prompt: Completa: (Yo) ___ a Barcelona el año pasado. (viajar, pretérito indefinido)
questions.explanation: Viajar is regular in the indefinido: viajé, viajaste, viajó…

questions.prompt: Completa: Empezaron a salir ___ tres años.
questions.explanation: 'Hace' plus a period of time expresses how long ago something started.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I had to do it yesterday.'
questions.explanation: Tener que plus infinitive: tuve que hacerlo, with the pronoun attached to the infinitive as learned in lesson 53.

activities.title: ¿Qué hiciste ayer?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Catch up on yesterday and a move to a new neighbourhood, exercising ayer, anoche, hace and en plus a year.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué hiciste ayer por la tarde?
lines.en: What did you do yesterday afternoon?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Fui al gimnasio y luego cené con unos amigos.
lines.en: I went to the gym and then had dinner with some friends.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y anoche saliste?
lines.en: And did you go out last night?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, anoche me quedé en casa viendo una película.
lines.en: No, last night I stayed home watching a movie.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cuándo os mudasteis a este barrio?
lines.en: When did you two move to this neighbourhood?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Nos mudamos hace dos años, en 2024.
lines.en: We moved two years ago, in 2024.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y dónde vivisteis antes?
lines.en: And where did you two live before?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vivimos en el centro, cerca de la estación, durante cinco años.
lines.en: We lived downtown, near the station, for five years.

days.title: Perfecto o indefinido: lo decide el marcador
days.objective: The learner can choose between the pretérito perfecto and the pretérito indefinido based on whether the time frame named is still open or already closed.
days.paretoFocus: This is the single most tested past-tense contrast at A2 and the marker-based rule works reliably without needing to judge how long ago something happened.
drills: Write two sentences about this week, one with este año (perfecto) and one with el año pasado (indefinido).
Explain out loud why 'hace un rato llamé' uses the indefinido even though it just happened.
Translate: 'This week I have slept badly, but last night I slept fine.'

items: What are the irregular participles of hacer, ver and escribir?
Which pronoun replaces 'a Ana' in 'la llamo a Ana'?
Give one marker that calls for the indefinido and one that calls for the perfecto.

activities.title: El contenedor de tiempo
activities.intro: The choice between perfecto and indefinido is not about how long ago something happened. It is about whether the time container the speaker names is still open when they speak (perfecto) or already closed (indefinido); markers are the reliable signal, and American Spanish generally uses the indefinido across the board where peninsular keeps this contrast, a variety difference rather than an error.

items.hr: Este año he viajado mucho.
items.en: This year I have travelled a lot.
items.note: 'este año' is a container still open when you speak, so perfecto: he viajado

items.hr: El año pasado viajé mucho.
items.en: Last year I travelled a lot.
items.note: 'el año pasado' is a container already closed, so indefinido: viajé, same amount of travel, different container

items.hr: Hace un rato llamé a mi madre.
items.en: A moment ago I called my mother.
items.note: even something very recent takes indefinido if the marker closes the container: 'hace un rato' names a finished instant, not an open period

items.hr: Esta semana he dormido fatal.
items.en: This week I have slept terribly.
items.note: 'esta semana' is still running, so perfecto, even though some of those nights are already several days in the past

items.hr: Hoy me he levantado tarde, pero ayer me levanté temprano.
items.en: Today I got up late, but yesterday I got up early.
items.note: same idea, two containers: 'hoy' is still open (perfecto), 'ayer' is closed (indefinido)

activities.title: ¿Perfecto o indefinido?
activities.intro: Practise choosing the right past tense using the time marker as the signal.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la opción correcta? 'Esta mañana ___ al médico.'
questions.explanation: 'Esta mañana' is still part of today, an open container, so the perfecto is correct.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la opción correcta? 'El mes pasado ___ de trabajo.'
questions.explanation: 'El mes pasado' is a closed container, so the indefinido is correct.

questions.prompt: Completa: Hace un rato ___ (ver, yo) a Marta en la calle.
questions.explanation: Even a very recent moment takes the indefinido when the marker closes the container: 'hace un rato' names a finished instant.

questions.prompt: Completa: Todavía no ___ (terminar, yo) el informe de este año. (perfecto)
questions.explanation: 'Este año' is still open, so the perfecto is correct, reinforced by 'todavía no'.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'This week I have called her three times.'
questions.explanation: 'Esta semana' is an open container, so the perfecto is used, with the direct object pronoun 'la' before the auxiliary.

activities.title: ¿Has estado alguna vez…?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk about travel this year and last year, contrasting the perfecto and the indefinido in the same conversation.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Has estado alguna vez en Alemania?
lines.en: Have you ever been to Germany?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, fui el año pasado, con mi hermana.
lines.en: Yes, I went last year, with my sister.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y este año has viajado a algún sitio?
lines.en: And this year have you travelled anywhere?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, este año he ido a Italia y a Francia.
lines.en: Yes, this year I've gone to Italy and France.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cuándo volviste de Francia?
lines.en: When did you get back from France?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Volví hace dos semanas, fue un viaje muy corto.
lines.en: I got back two weeks ago, it was a very short trip.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Has probado la comida portuguesa alguna vez?
lines.en: Have you ever tried Portuguese food?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, la probé el año pasado en Lisboa y me gustó mucho.
lines.en: Yes, I tried it last year in Lisbon and I liked it a lot.

days.title: El pretérito imperfecto: hablaba, comía
days.objective: The learner can form the imperfecto for regular -ar and -er/-ir verbs and for the only three irregular verbs in the whole language: ser, ir and ver.
days.paretoFocus: The imperfecto has almost no irregularity, unusually good news after the irregular indefinido, and it is essential for describing and narrating.
drills: Conjugate hablar, comer and vivir fully in the imperfecto.
Recite the six forms of ser, ir and ver in the imperfecto from memory.
Translate: 'When I was little, we used to go to the beach every summer.'

items: What is the pretérito indefinido marker that closes a time container, from lesson 67?
Give the indefinido of ir in the yo form.
Recall one irregular participle from lesson 57.

activities.title: Solo tres verbos irregulares
activities.intro: Of all the verbs in Spanish, only three are irregular in the imperfecto: ser, ir and ver. Every other verb, however irregular it is elsewhere, is completely regular here, which makes the imperfecto the easiest tense to form in the whole language.

items.hr: De niño, hablaba mucho por teléfono.
items.en: As a child, I used to talk on the phone a lot.
items.note: -ar verbs: hablaba, hablabas, hablaba, hablábamos, hablabais, hablaban

items.hr: Comíamos juntos todos los domingos.
items.en: We used to eat together every Sunday.
items.note: -er/-ir verbs share endings: comía, comías, comía, comíamos, comíais, comían (vivía follows the same pattern)

items.hr: Cuando era pequeño, era muy tímido.
items.en: When I was little, I was very shy.
items.note: ser: era, eras, era, éramos, erais, eran, the only irregular verb that keeps -er/-ir style endings

items.hr: Cada verano íbamos a la playa.
items.en: Every summer we used to go to the beach.
items.note: ir: iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, ibais, iban

items.hr: Antes no veía mucho la televisión.
items.en: Before, I didn't use to watch much television.
items.note: ver: veía, veías, veía, veíamos, veíais, veían (keeps the e of the stem, unlike other -er verbs)

activities.title: Solo tres irregulares
activities.intro: Practise the regular imperfecto endings and the three irregular verbs ser, ir and ver.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma de 'nosotros' del imperfecto de 'ser'?
questions.explanation: Ser's imperfecto stem is er-, so éramos is the nosotros form; somos is present, fuimos is indefinido, erais is vosotros.

questions.prompt: ¿Cómo se dice 'we used to go' (ir, imperfecto)?
questions.explanation: Ir's imperfecto: iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, ibais, iban; fuimos is indefinido, vamos is present, and 'íbais' is a misspelling: the real vosotros form, ibais, carries no accent.

questions.prompt: Completa: De pequeña, (yo) ___ mucho al fútbol. (jugar, imperfecto)
questions.explanation: Regular -ar imperfecto: jugaba, jugabas, jugaba…

questions.prompt: Completa: Mis abuelos ___ en un pueblo pequeño. (vivir, imperfecto)
questions.explanation: Regular -ir imperfecto: vivía, vivías…vivían.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'We used to see each other every weekend.'
questions.explanation: Ver's imperfecto keeps the stem vowel: veíamos; 'nos' marks the reciprocal action, as learned with reflexives.

activities.title: ¿Cómo eras de pequeño?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk about what you were like and did as a child, exercising era, hablaba, íbamos and veías.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cómo eras de pequeño?
lines.en: What were you like as a kid?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Era bastante tímido y hablaba poco.
lines.en: I was quite shy and I didn't talk much.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué hacíais los fines de semana?
lines.en: What did you all use to do on weekends?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Íbamos al parque y jugábamos al fútbol con los vecinos.
lines.en: We used to go to the park and play football with the neighbours.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Veías mucho la tele de niño?
lines.en: Did you watch a lot of TV as a kid?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, casi no veía la tele, prefería leer cómics.
lines.en: No, I hardly watched TV, I preferred reading comics.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Vivíais cerca del colegio?
lines.en: Did you all live near the school?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, vivíamos a cinco minutos, íbamos andando siempre.
lines.en: Yes, we lived five minutes away, we always walked there.

days.title: Describir en el pasado: personas, lugares y tiempo
days.objective: The learner can use the imperfecto to describe people, places, weather, clock time and age in the past.
days.paretoFocus: Description is the imperfecto's core job and appears in every narrative task the exam sets.
drills: Describe a grandparent's appearance and personality in the imperfecto.
Say the weather and the time in three past scenes.
Translate: 'I was ten years old when it was raining so hard we couldn't leave.'

items: Give the imperfecto of ser in the yo form.
What construction expresses age with tener, from lesson 26?
Recall a marker that closes a time container, from lesson 67.

activities.title: Era, tenía, hacía…
activities.intro: The imperfecto is the tense for backdrop, not action: what someone looked like, what the sky was doing, what the clock said, how old someone was. None of these are single completed events, so none take the indefinido.

items.hr: Mi abuela era muy alta y tenía el pelo blanco.
items.en: My grandmother was very tall and had white hair.
items.note: physical description in the past: era, tenía

items.hr: La casa tenía un jardín enorme.
items.en: The house had a huge garden.
items.note: describing a place: tenía

items.hr: Hacía mucho frío esa noche.
items.en: It was very cold that night.
items.note: weather in the past: hacía frío, calor, sol, viento

items.hr: Eran las cinco de la tarde cuando llegamos.
items.en: It was five in the afternoon when we arrived.
items.note: clock time in the past is always imperfecto: era la una, eran las dos…

items.hr: Yo tenía diez años cuando empecé a nadar.
items.en: I was ten years old when I started swimming.
items.note: age in the past: tenía + años, never the perfecto or indefinido

activities.title: Describir personas, lugares y tiempo
activities.intro: Fill in the correct imperfecto form for a series of scene-setting descriptions.

questions.prompt: ¿Cómo se dice 'it was raining' en imperfecto?
questions.explanation: Weather description takes the imperfecto; llovió is indefinido (a finished shower), ha llovido is perfecto, llueve is present.

questions.prompt: Elige la opción correcta: 'Cuando (yo) ___ pequeño, mi calle no tenía nombre.'
questions.explanation: Describing an ongoing state, being a child, takes the imperfecto.

questions.prompt: Completa: ___ las ocho de la mañana cuando sonó el despertador. (ser, imperfecto)
questions.explanation: Clock time in the past is always imperfecto: eran las ocho.

questions.prompt: Completa: Mi padre ___ treinta años cuando yo nací. (tener, imperfecto)
questions.explanation: Age in the past uses tener in the imperfecto: tenía treinta años.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'The house was old, but I really liked it.'
questions.explanation: Era describes the state of the house; 'me gustaba' reuses the gustar construction from lesson 38, now in the imperfecto.

activities.title: ¿Cómo era tu barrio?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Describe a childhood neighbourhood, the weather, a specific moment and your age at the time.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cómo era tu barrio de pequeño?
lines.en: What was your neighbourhood like when you were little?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Era tranquilo y tenía muchos árboles.
lines.en: It was quiet and had a lot of trees.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué tiempo hacía normalmente en invierno?
lines.en: What was the weather usually like in winter?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Hacía bastante frío y a veces nevaba.
lines.en: It was quite cold and sometimes it snowed.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué hora era cuando llegasteis ayer?
lines.en: What time was it when you all arrived yesterday?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Eran casi las once de la noche.
lines.en: It was almost eleven at night.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cuántos años tenías cuando os mudasteis allí?
lines.en: How old were you when you all moved there?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tenía solo seis años, casi no me acuerdo.
lines.en: I was only six years old, I barely remember.

days.title: Costumbres de antes: iba todos los días…
days.objective: The learner can describe repeated past habits with the imperfecto and contrast them with the present using antes and ahora.
days.paretoFocus: Describing how life used to be is the conversation an adult learner is asked for again and again, and the imperfecto is the only tense that can carry it.
drills: Write three sentences about a habit you had as a teenager.
Contrast one old habit and one current one using antes/ahora.
Translate: 'Before we used to go out every Friday; now we hardly ever go out.'

items: Give the reflexive conjugation of levantarse in the present, from lesson 47.
Recall the imperfecto of ir in the nosotros form.
What word pair opens and closes the antes/ahora contrast?

activities.title: Antes… ahora…
activities.intro: A habit that happened repeatedly over an unspecified stretch of the past, like walking to school every day, is imperfecto; the contrast word antes signals it, and ahora switches back to the present to show what changed.

items.hr: Antes iba todos los días al colegio andando.
items.en: Before, I used to walk to school every day.
items.note: habitual action: iba + todos los días

items.hr: Ahora voy en autobús.
items.en: Now I go by bus.
items.note: ahora + present tense contrasts with the imperfecto habit

items.hr: De joven, fumaba mucho.
items.en: When I was young, I used to smoke a lot.
items.note: fumar -> fumaba, a dropped habit

items.hr: Antes salíamos todos los viernes; ahora casi nunca salimos.
items.en: Before we used to go out every Friday; now we hardly ever go out.
items.note: antes + imperfecto vs ahora + present, the standard contrast pair

items.hr: Mi madre siempre me despertaba a las siete.
items.en: My mother always used to wake me up at seven.
items.note: siempre + imperfecto for an invariable habit

activities.title: Hábitos de antes
activities.intro: Practise expressing repeated past habits and contrasting them with the present.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué frase expresa un hábito del pasado?
options: Iba al gimnasio todos los días
questions.answer: Iba al gimnasio todos los días
questions.explanation: Repeated, habitual actions in the past use the imperfecto; the others describe single or present events.

questions.prompt: Elige la opción correcta: 'Antes (nosotros) ___ mucho café; ahora casi no tomamos.'
questions.explanation: A repeated past habit takes the imperfecto: tomábamos.

questions.prompt: Completa: De pequeños, mis hermanos y yo ___ (jugar, imperfecto) en la calle.
questions.explanation: Regular -ar imperfecto, nosotros form: jugábamos.

questions.prompt: Completa: Antes ella ___ (trabajar, imperfecto) los sábados.
questions.explanation: Regular -ar imperfecto, ella form: trabajaba.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I used to get up early, but now I get up late.'
questions.explanation: Reflexive levantarse from lesson 47 in the imperfecto (me levantaba) contrasted with the present (me levanto).

activities.title: Antes y ahora
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Compare childhood summers with life now, exercising iba, cocinaba and the antes/ahora contrast.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué hacías los veranos de pequeño?
lines.en: What did you do in the summers as a kid?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Iba todos los días a la piscina con mis primos.
lines.en: I used to go to the pool every day with my cousins.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y ahora qué haces en verano?
lines.en: And what do you do now in summer?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ahora trabajo casi todo el verano, así que salgo poco.
lines.en: Now I work almost the whole summer, so I go out little.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Tus padres cocinaban mucho antes?
lines.en: Did your parents used to cook a lot?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, mi madre cocinaba todos los días, ahora pedimos comida a veces.
lines.en: Yes, my mother used to cook every day, now we order food sometimes.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Ibais de vacaciones cada año?
lines.en: Did you all use to go on holiday every year?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, siempre íbamos al mismo pueblo de la costa.
lines.en: Yes, we always used to go to the same coastal village.

days.title: Recuerdos de infancia
days.objective: The learner can narrate a block of childhood memories using the imperfecto for description, habits, feelings and states.
days.paretoFocus: Consolidating a whole paragraph in one tense builds the confidence needed before contrasting it with the indefinido in the next lesson.
drills: Write five sentences about your own childhood using only the imperfecto.
Describe one thing you really liked doing as a child with me gustaba mucho.
Translate: 'My grandfather used to tell me stories at night.'

items: Recall the indirect object pronoun used with gustar-class verbs for 'to me'.
Give the imperfecto of tener in the yo form.
What is the peninsular word for 'flat, apartment' that contrasts with Latin American 'departamento'?

activities.title: Cuando era niña…
activities.intro: A whole memory, not just one sentence, can stay in the imperfecto: description, habits, likes and fears about a period of your life all belong here.

items.hr: Cuando era niña, vivía en un pueblo pequeño.
items.en: When I was a girl, I lived in a small village.
items.note: era + vivía, both imperfecto, describing a period

items.hr: Mis abuelos tenían una granja con animales.
items.en: My grandparents had a farm with animals.
items.note: tenían describes a lasting fact

items.hr: Los domingos comíamos todos juntos en casa de la abuela.
items.en: On Sundays we all used to eat together at grandma's house.
items.note: comíamos, a repeated Sunday habit

items.hr: Me gustaba mucho subirme a los árboles.
items.en: I really liked climbing trees.
items.note: gustar in the imperfecto: me gustaba + infinitivo

items.hr: Tenía miedo de la oscuridad.
items.en: I was afraid of the dark.
items.note: tener miedo de = to be afraid of

activities.title: Un párrafo de infancia
activities.intro: Practise a whole passage of childhood description and habits in the imperfecto.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué frase describe mejor un recuerdo de infancia?
options: He jugado en el jardín hoy
Jugaba en el jardín todas las tardes
questions.answer: Jugaba en el jardín todas las tardes
questions.explanation: A general childhood memory, repeated over years, needs the imperfecto.

questions.prompt: Elige la opción correcta: 'De niño, me ___ los animales.' (gustar)
questions.explanation: Gustar in the imperfecto agrees with the plural subject 'los animales': gustaban.

questions.prompt: Completa: Mi abuelo me ___ (contar, imperfecto) historias por la noche.
questions.explanation: Regular -ar imperfecto: contaba.

questions.prompt: Completa: De pequeño, le ___ (tener, imperfecto) miedo al perro del vecino.
questions.explanation: Tener in the imperfecto, yo form: tenía; 'le' reviews the indirect object pronoun from lesson 51.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'We used to spend the summers at my grandparents' house.'
questions.explanation: Regular -ar imperfecto, nosotros form: pasábamos, for a repeated summer habit.

activities.title: El pueblo de mis abuelos
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Share childhood summer memories, exercising pasaba, gustaba, tenía and jugábamos.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Dónde pasabas los veranos de pequeño?
lines.en: Where did you spend your summers as a kid?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Los pasaba en el pueblo de mis abuelos, cerca de las montañas.
lines.en: I spent them in my grandparents' village, near the mountains.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué te gustaba hacer allí?
lines.en: What did you like to do there?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Me gustaba mucho montar en bici y bañarme en el río.
lines.en: I really liked riding my bike and swimming in the river.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Tenías hermanos para jugar?
lines.en: Did you have siblings to play with?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, tenía dos hermanos y siempre jugábamos juntos al escondite.
lines.en: Yes, I had two siblings and we always played hide and seek together.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Echabas de menos a tus amigos de la ciudad?
lines.en: Did you miss your friends from the city?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Un poco, pero hacía nuevos amigos allí cada verano.
lines.en: A little, but I made new friends there every summer.

days.title: Imperfecto o indefinido: el fondo y el suceso
days.objective: The learner can distinguish background description (imperfecto) from the single event that interrupts it (indefinido) in a narrative, and reconstruct a story using both.
days.paretoFocus: This is the single most important past-tense contrast at A2, tested constantly in narration and reading comprehension.
drills: Write a two-clause sentence with a background in imperfecto and an event in indefinido.
Say out loud what 'Llovía cuando salí' actually describes, step by step.
Translate: 'The children were playing when it started to rain.'

items: Give the indefinido of ver in the yo form.
Recall the direct object pronoun for a feminine singular noun.
What did lesson 68 call the deciding factor between perfecto and indefinido?

activities.title: Llovía cuando salí
activities.intro: Reconstruct this: the background of a story, what was already true or already happening, is imperfecto. The one thing that actually happens, the event that moves the story forward, is indefinido. 'Llovía cuando salí' means the rain was already falling (background) and leaving was the one thing that happened (event); the two tenses in the same sentence do different jobs.

items.hr: Llovía cuando salí de casa.
items.en: It was raining when I left the house.
items.note: llovía = the background scene, already in progress; salí = the single event that happens inside it

items.hr: Dormía cuando sonó el teléfono.
items.en: I was sleeping when the phone rang.
items.note: the ongoing state (dormía) is interrupted by the sudden event (sonó)

items.hr: Hacía sol, así que decidimos ir a la playa.
items.en: It was sunny, so we decided to go to the beach.
items.note: hacía sol sets the scene; decidimos is the one thing that happened

items.hr: Había mucha gente en la calle cuando llegamos.
items.en: There were a lot of people in the street when we arrived.
items.note: había (imperfecto of hay) describes the scene; llegamos is the event

items.hr: Estaba muy cansado, pero fui a la fiesta igualmente.
items.en: I was very tired, but I went to the party anyway.
items.note: estaba describes an ongoing state; fui is the single completed action

activities.title: El fondo y el suceso
activities.intro: For each sentence, decide which clause sets the scene and which one interrupts it.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué tiempo describe el fondo de una escena?
questions.explanation: Description that was already true when the story starts is the imperfecto's job.

questions.prompt: Elige la opción correcta: 'Yo ___ la cena cuando se fue la luz.'
questions.explanation: The cooking was already in progress, the background, when the power went out, the event, se fue.

questions.prompt: Completa: (Nosotros) ___ (ver) la película cuando se cortó internet. (imperfecto)
questions.explanation: The film was already playing, the background: veíamos.

questions.prompt: Completa: Yo ___ (caminar, imperfecto) por el parque cuando la vi.
questions.explanation: The walk was the background, in progress when the single event, la vi, happened.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'The children were playing when it started to rain.'
questions.explanation: Jugaban is the background, empezó is the single event that interrupts it.

activities.title: Cuéntame qué pasó
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Reconstruct yesterday's story, weaving background (imperfecto) and events (indefinido) together, starting with the canonical 'llovía cuando salí'.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Cuéntame qué pasó ayer, empieza por el principio.
lines.en: Tell me what happened yesterday, start from the beginning.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Llovía cuando salí de casa, así que cogí el paraguas.
lines.en: It was raining when I left the house, so I took the umbrella.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y luego qué pasó?
lines.en: And then what happened?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Caminaba hacia el metro cuando vi a Marta en la esquina.
lines.en: I was walking toward the metro when I saw Marta on the corner.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué hacía ella allí?
lines.en: What was she doing there?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Esperaba el autobús, pero al final vino conmigo en metro.
lines.en: She was waiting for the bus, but in the end she came with me on the metro.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y cómo terminó la tarde?
lines.en: And how did the afternoon end?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Cuando llegamos a la oficina, ya no llovía, así que dejamos el paraguas en la entrada.
lines.en: When we got to the office, it wasn't raining anymore, so we left the umbrella at the entrance.

days.title: Las tres formas del pasado: un solo procedimiento
days.objective: The learner can apply one step-by-step procedure to choose among perfecto, indefinido and imperfecto for any past sentence.
days.paretoFocus: Having one procedure instead of three separate rules is what lets a learner actually produce correct past tense under time pressure.
drills: Walk through the three-step procedure out loud using your own example sentence.
Write one sentence that uses all three past tenses correctly.
Translate: 'I have never been to Peru, but I did go to Chile two years ago.'

items: Recall the marker 'todavía no' and which tense it usually pairs with.
Give the indirect object pronoun for 'to him, to her'.
What is the canonical pair from lesson 73 for background and event?

activities.title: Un procedimiento, tres pasos
activities.intro: Instead of three separate rules, use one procedure: first ask if it is a description or a habit (imperfecto); if not, ask if the marker closes the time frame (indefinido) or leaves it open (perfecto); and within one story, remember background is imperfecto and the event that interrupts it is indefinido.

items.hr: Paso uno: ¿es una descripción o un hábito? Si es así, imperfecto: 'Cuando era joven, viajaba mucho.'
items.en: Step one: is it a description or a habit? If so, imperfecto: 'When I was young, I used to travel a lot.'

items.hr: Paso dos: ¿es un hecho puntual y el marcador cierra el tiempo? Indefinido: 'El verano pasado viajé a Grecia.'
items.en: Step two: is it a single fact and does the marker close the time frame? Indefinido: 'Last summer I travelled to Greece.'

items.hr: Paso tres: ¿el marcador todavía está abierto? Perfecto: 'Este verano he viajado a Grecia.'
items.en: Step three: is the marker's time frame still open? Perfecto: 'This summer I have travelled to Greece.'

items.hr: En una misma historia, el fondo va en imperfecto y el hecho que lo interrumpe va en indefinido: 'Hacía calor cuando llegamos.'
items.en: Within one story, the background goes in imperfecto and the event that interrupts it goes in indefinido: 'It was hot when we arrived.'

items.hr: Los tres juntos: 'Este mes he viajado dos veces; la última vez fui a Roma, y allí hacía un frío horrible.'
items.en: All three together: 'This month I have travelled twice; the last time I went to Rome, and there it was horribly cold.'
items.note: he viajado (open container) / fui (closed single fact) / hacía (background description)

activities.title: El procedimiento en acción
activities.intro: Practise applying the three-step procedure to choose the correct past tense.

questions.prompt: En la frase 'Hacía sol cuando salimos', ¿qué función tiene 'hacía'?
options: describe el fondo de la escena
questions.answer: describe el fondo de la escena
questions.explanation: Hacía sets the ongoing background against which salimos, the single event, happens.

questions.prompt: Elige la opción correcta para completar el procedimiento: 'Este año ___ tres exámenes; el último lo hice ayer.'
questions.explanation: 'Este año' is still open, so perfecto for the general statement, while 'ayer' closes the specific instance.

questions.prompt: Completa: Cuando (yo) ___ (llegar, indefinido) a casa, mi hermana ya dormía.
questions.explanation: Llegar in the indefinido, yo form: llegué, the single event.

questions.prompt: Completa: Todavía no le ___ (decir, yo) la verdad a mi hermano. (perfecto)
questions.explanation: 'Todavía no' pairs with the perfecto: he dicho, with the irregular participle from lesson 57.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I have never been to Peru, but I did go to Chile two years ago.'
questions.explanation: Nunca he estado is perfecto, life-experience; fui hace dos años is indefinido, a closed instance.

activities.title: Un solo procedimiento
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Move fluidly among all three past tenses talking about travel.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Has estado alguna vez en Asia?
lines.en: Have you ever been to Asia?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, nunca he estado, pero fui a Marruecos hace tres años.
lines.en: No, I've never been, but I went to Morocco three years ago.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué tal fue el viaje?
lines.en: How was the trip?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Fue increíble. Hacía mucho calor y la gente era muy amable.
lines.en: It was incredible. It was very hot and the people were very kind.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y este año tienes planes de viajar?
lines.en: And this year do you have travel plans?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, este año ya he viajado dos veces y en agosto voy a Portugal.
lines.en: Yes, this year I've already travelled twice and in August I'm going to Portugal.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué hacías normalmente cuando viajabas de joven?
lines.en: What did you usually do when you travelled when young?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Viajaba con poco dinero y siempre dormía en albergues.
lines.en: I travelled with little money and always slept in hostels.

days.title: Contar una historia: primero, luego, después…
days.objective: The learner can sequence a past narrative using the standard connectors of Spanish storytelling.
days.paretoFocus: Connectors turn a list of past-tense sentences into an actual story, and they are reused constantly in the exam's writing tasks.
drills: Retell your morning using primero, luego and después.
Write one sentence with de repente to introduce an unexpected event.
Translate: 'First we visited the museum, then we ate at a small restaurant.'

items: Give the imperfecto of estar in the nosotros form.
Recall one marker from lesson 67 that always calls for the indefinido.
What tense does 'de repente' pair with, and why?

activities.title: Primero… luego… al final
activities.intro: A short set of connectors sequences a story from start to finish: primero and luego open it, después and entonces continue it, de repente marks a surprise, and al final closes it.

items.hr: Primero desayunamos y luego salimos de casa.
items.en: First we had breakfast and then we left the house.
items.note: primero…luego, the basic sequence

items.hr: Después fuimos a la estación.
items.en: Afterwards we went to the station.
items.note: después = afterwards, next

items.hr: Entonces nos dimos cuenta de que era muy tarde.
items.en: At that point we realised it was very late.
items.note: entonces = at that point, then, a logical or temporal link

items.hr: De repente empezó a llover muchísimo.
items.en: Suddenly it started raining a lot.
items.note: de repente = suddenly, marks an unexpected event, always indefinido

items.hr: Al final llegamos justo a tiempo.
items.en: In the end we arrived just in time.
items.note: al final = in the end, closes the narrative

activities.title: Conectores de la narración
activities.intro: Practise sequencing a story with primero, luego, después, entonces, de repente and al final.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué conector introduce un hecho inesperado?
questions.explanation: De repente marks a sudden, unexpected turn in the story.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué conector cierra una historia?
questions.explanation: Al final closes the narrative sequence.

questions.prompt: Completa: Primero cenamos y ___ vimos una película.
questions.explanation: Luego continues the sequence right after primero.

questions.prompt: Completa: Estábamos en la calle cuando, ___, empezó a nevar.
questions.explanation: De repente marks the unexpected turn, inside a background already set by estábamos.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'First we visited the museum, then we ate at a small restaurant.'
questions.explanation: Primero opens the sequence, luego continues it.

activities.title: El sábado
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Narrate a Saturday using the full set of story connectors.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué hicisteis el sábado?
lines.en: What did you all do on Saturday?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Primero fuimos al mercado, luego paseamos por el centro.
lines.en: First we went to the market, then we walked around downtown.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y después?
lines.en: And afterwards?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Después comimos en una terraza, hacía muy buen tiempo.
lines.en: Afterwards we ate on a terrace, the weather was very good.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Pasó algo interesante?
lines.en: Did anything interesting happen?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, de repente empezó a sonar música en la plaza, era un concierto sorpresa.
lines.en: Yes, suddenly music started playing in the square, it was a surprise concert.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cómo terminó el día?
lines.en: How did the day end?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Al final nos quedamos escuchando hasta las diez de la noche.
lines.en: In the end we stayed listening until ten at night.

days.title: Una historia contada dos veces
days.objective: The learner can retell the same past story twice, once briefly and once with full background detail, moving fluidly among perfecto, indefinido and imperfecto.
days.paretoFocus: Consolidating the whole past-tense system before moving to the imperative locks in the highest-value grammar of the level.
drills: Tell a short version of a recent mishap using only indefinido.
Retell it with background detail using imperfecto too.
Translate: 'I was very tired, so I didn't hear the alarm clock.'

items: Give the reflexive form of despertarse in the indefinido, yo form.
Recall a connector from lesson 75 that closes a narrative.
What does 'esta semana' signal about tense choice, from lesson 68?

activities.title: Corta y larga
activities.intro: The same event can be told as bare facts, indefinido only, or with full background and cause, mixing in imperfecto and perfecto; both versions are correct, they just serve different purposes.

items.hr: Versión corta: Ayer perdí el tren y llegué tarde al trabajo.
items.en: Short version: Yesterday I missed the train and arrived late to work.
items.note: the bare facts, indefinido only

items.hr: Versión larga: Ayer me desperté tarde porque el despertador no sonó, así que perdí el tren y llegué tarde al trabajo.
items.en: Long version: Yesterday I woke up late because the alarm didn't go off, so I missed the train and arrived late to work.
items.note: cause added, still all indefinido because each fact is a single event

items.hr: Con fondo: Estaba muy cansado esa mañana, y por eso no oí el despertador.
items.en: With background: I was very tired that morning, and that's why I didn't hear the alarm.
items.note: estaba = background state that explains the event

items.hr: Esta semana ya me ha pasado dos veces.
items.en: This week it has already happened to me twice.
items.note: perfecto for something inside the still-open week

items.hr: Al final, llegué solo diez minutos tarde y nadie se enfadó.
items.en: In the end, I was only ten minutes late and nobody got annoyed.
items.note: al final closes the story; se enfadó reviews the pronominal verb group

activities.title: La misma historia, dos veces
activities.intro: Practise moving among all three past tenses to tell the same story briefly and then in full.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué versión de una historia usa solo indefinido?
options: la versión con una experiencia general
la versión de los hechos puros
la versión con una descripción del tiempo
la versión con el fondo de la escena
questions.answer: la versión de los hechos puros
questions.explanation: A bare sequence of single completed facts uses only the indefinido.

questions.prompt: Elige la opción correcta: 'Aquella mañana (yo) ___ muy cansado.'
questions.explanation: Describing a state that explains what happened next is imperfecto.

questions.prompt: Completa: (Yo) me ___ (despertar, indefinido) porque el despertador no sonó.
questions.explanation: Reflexive despertarse in the indefinido, yo form: me desperté.

questions.prompt: Completa: Esta semana ya me ___ (pasar, perfecto) dos veces lo mismo.
questions.explanation: 'Esta semana' is still open, so the perfecto is correct: ha pasado.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I was very tired, so I didn't hear the alarm clock.'
questions.explanation: Estaba sets the background state; no oí is the single event it explains.

activities.title: Otra vez, con detalles
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Retell yesterday's mishap with full background detail this time.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Cuéntame otra vez qué pasó ayer, con todos los detalles.
lines.en: Tell me again what happened yesterday, with all the details.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale. Estaba muy cansado esa noche y me acosté tarde.
lines.en: Okay. I was very tired that night and I went to bed late.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y por eso llegaste tarde?
lines.en: And that's why you were late?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, no oí el despertador porque dormí muy poco esa noche.
lines.en: Yes, I didn't hear the alarm because I slept very little that night.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y qué hiciste al darte cuenta?
lines.en: And what did you do when you realised?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Me vestí rapidísimo y salí corriendo hacia la estación.
lines.en: I got dressed super fast and ran out toward the station.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Llegaste a tiempo al final?
lines.en: Did you make it on time in the end?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No del todo, llegué diez minutos tarde, pero mi jefe no se enfadó.
lines.en: Not quite, I arrived ten minutes late, but my boss didn't get annoyed.

days.title: El imperativo afirmativo: tú y vosotros
days.objective: The learner can form the regular affirmative imperative for tú and vosotros and use the peninsular vosotros form naturally.
days.paretoFocus: Giving direct instructions and requests is a core everyday function, and vosotros is a live, tested part of peninsular grammar.
drills: Give three commands to a friend using the tú imperative.
Give the same three commands to a group using vosotros.
Translate: 'Open the door, please.'

items: Recall the perfecto and indefinido forms of hacer in the yo form.
What is the peninsular plural form used for a group of friends, from lesson 14?
Give the imperfecto of hacer in the nosotros form.

activities.title: Habla, come, escribe / hablad, comed, escribid
activities.intro: The tú imperative of regular verbs is identical to the él/ella present form; the vosotros imperative simply replaces the infinitive's final -r with -d, and it has no irregulars at all, in any verb.

items.hr: ¡Habla más despacio, por favor!
items.en: Speak more slowly, please!
items.note: tú imperative of -ar verbs = same as the él/ella present form: habla

items.hr: ¡Come un poco más!
items.en: Eat a little more!
items.note: tú imperative of -er verbs = come

items.hr: ¡Escribe tu nombre aquí!
items.en: Write your name here!
items.note: tú imperative of -ir verbs = escribe

items.hr: ¡Hablad más alto, no os oigo!
items.en: Speak louder, I can't hear you!
items.note: vosotros imperative: change the infinitive's final -r to -d: hablar -> hablad

items.hr: ¡Comed y bebed, la comida está lista!
items.en: Eat and drink, the food is ready!
items.note: comer -> comed, beber -> bebed; the vosotros imperative has no irregulars

activities.title: El imperativo regular
activities.intro: Practise the regular tú and vosotros affirmative imperative.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es el imperativo de 'tú' para 'escribir'?
questions.explanation: -ir verbs form the tú imperative like the él/ella present: escribe; escribid is vosotros, escribí is indefinido yo.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es el imperativo de 'vosotros' para 'trabajar'?
questions.explanation: Vosotros imperative = infinitive minus -r plus -d: trabajad.

questions.prompt: Completa: ¡___ (leer, tú) este párrafo en voz alta!
questions.explanation: Tú imperative of leer, like the él/ella present: lee.

questions.prompt: Completa: ¡___ (abrir, vosotros) las ventanas, hace calor!
questions.explanation: Vosotros imperative of abrir: infinitive minus -r plus -d: abrid.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Open the door, please.'
questions.explanation: Abre is the tú imperative of abrir, identical to the él/ella present form.

activities.title: La mudanza
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Direct a group helping with a move, exercising both the tú and vosotros regular imperative.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Necesito ayuda con la mudanza, ¿puedes venir?
lines.en: I need help with the move, can you come?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro, ¿qué hago primero?
lines.en: Sure, what should I do first?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Lleva esas cajas al salón, por favor.
lines.en: Take those boxes to the living room, please.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, ¿y qué más?
lines.en: Okay, and what else?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Habla con tu hermano, necesitamos más ayuda.
lines.en: Talk to your brother, we need more help.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: ¡Venid vosotros también, hay mucho que hacer!
lines.en: You all come too, there's a lot to do!

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Escribid la lista de lo que falta en la cocina.
lines.en: Write down the list of what's missing in the kitchen.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Perfecto, empezad vosotros con las cajas grandes y yo empiezo con las pequeñas.
lines.en: Perfect, you all start with the big boxes and I'll start with the small ones.

days.title: Imperativos irregulares de tú
days.objective: The learner can produce the eight irregular tú imperatives by heart: di, haz, pon, sal, ten, ven, sé and ve.
days.paretoFocus: These eight verbs are among the most frequent in spoken instructions, so their irregular forms have to be automatic.
drills: Recite all eight irregular tú imperatives in one breath.
Give three commands to a child using three different irregular forms.
Translate: 'Come here and tell the truth.'

items: Give the tú imperative of hablar and comer, from lesson 77.
Recall the vosotros imperative of escribir.
What is 'sé' as an imperative, and how is it different in spelling from 'se'?

activities.title: Di, haz, pon, sal, ten, ven, sé, ve
activities.intro: Eight very common verbs have a short, irregular tú imperative that has to be memorised as a set, since it does not follow the regular pattern.

items.hr: ¡Di la verdad y ven aquí!
items.en: Tell the truth and come here!
items.note: decir -> di; venir -> ven

items.hr: ¡Haz los deberes y pon la mesa!
items.en: Do your homework and set the table!
items.note: hacer -> haz; poner -> pon

items.hr: ¡Sal de aquí y ten cuidado con el coche!
items.en: Get out of here and be careful with the car!
items.note: salir -> sal; tener -> ten

items.hr: ¡Sé bueno con tu hermana!
items.en: Be good to your sister!
items.note: ser -> sé (written with an accent to distinguish it from 'se')

items.hr: ¡Ve a la tienda y compra pan!
items.en: Go to the shop and buy bread!
items.note: ir -> ve; compra is regular (comprar -> compra)

activities.title: Los ocho irregulares
activities.intro: Match each infinitive to its short, memorised tú command form.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es el imperativo de 'tú' para 'hacer'?
questions.explanation: Hacer's irregular tú imperative is haz.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es el imperativo de 'tú' para 'tener'?
questions.explanation: Tener's irregular tú imperative is ten.

questions.prompt: Completa: ¡___ (poner, tú) tu abrigo, hace frío!
questions.explanation: Poner's irregular tú imperative is pon.

questions.prompt: Completa: ¡___ (ser, tú) puntual mañana!
questions.explanation: Ser's irregular tú imperative is sé, always written with an accent.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Come here and tell the truth.'
questions.explanation: Ven (venir) and di (decir) are two of the eight irregular tú imperatives.

activities.title: Antes de salir
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Give a child a set of instructions before they go out, exercising the eight irregular imperatives.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Mamá, ¿puedo salir a jugar?
lines.en: Mum, can I go out to play?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, pero antes haz los deberes.
lines.en: Yes, but first do your homework.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vale, ya los hago. ¿Y luego?
lines.en: Okay, I'm doing them. And then?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Luego pon la mesa, vamos a cenar pronto.
lines.en: Then set the table, we're going to have dinner soon.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Puedo invitar a mi amigo?
lines.en: Can I invite my friend?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro, pero sé responsable y ten cuidado en la calle.
lines.en: Sure, but be responsible and be careful on the street.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Voy a comprar el pan primero?
lines.en: Should I go buy the bread first?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, ve a la panadería y di que es para nosotros.
lines.en: Yes, go to the bakery and say it's for us.

days.title: El imperativo de usted y ustedes
days.objective: The learner can form the usted and ustedes imperative from the yo-stem and use it in formal requests.
days.paretoFocus: Formal register, in shops, offices and with strangers, requires this form constantly, even though it comes from a structure not taught until B1.
drills: Give three formal instructions using usted.
Give the same three instructions to a group using ustedes.
Translate: 'Wait here, please, and be patient.'

items: Give the tú imperative of venir, from lesson 78.
Recall the yo-form present of tener and poner.
What register uses usted instead of tú, from lesson 14?

activities.title: Hable, coma, escriba
activities.intro: Formal commands are built the same way regardless of who you address: take the present-tense yo-form, drop the -o, then add -e for -ar verbs or -a for -er and -ir verbs. That swapped ending is actually the present subjunctive, which gets its full treatment at B1, so for now just memorise the shape.

items.hr: Hable más despacio, por favor.
items.en: Speak more slowly, please.
items.note: usted imperative: take the yo-form (hablo), drop the -o, add -e: hable

items.hr: Coma despacio, no hay prisa.
items.en: Eat slowly, there's no rush.
items.note: usted imperative of -er verbs: como -> coma

items.hr: Escriba su nombre aquí, por favor.
items.en: Write your name here, please.
items.note: usted imperative of -ir verbs: escribo -> escriba

items.hr: Pongan sus maletas aquí.
items.en: Put your suitcases here.
items.note: ustedes imperative adds -n to the usted form: ponga -> pongan, from pongo, the irregular yo-stem

items.hr: Tengan paciencia, el tren llega en cinco minutos.
items.en: Be patient, the train arrives in five minutes.
items.note: tengan, from tengo; the yo-stem irregularity carries over into the whole formal imperative

activities.title: Formas formales
activities.intro: Turn each yo-form present into a polite command for one person and then for several.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es el imperativo de 'usted' para 'hablar'?
questions.explanation: Usted imperative: yo-form hablo, drop -o, add -e: hable.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es el imperativo de 'ustedes' para 'tener'?
questions.explanation: Ustedes imperative from the irregular yo-stem tengo: tengan.

questions.prompt: Completa: ___ (esperar, usted) un momento, por favor.
questions.explanation: Usted imperative: yo-form espero, drop -o, add -e: espere.

questions.prompt: Completa: ___ (venir, ustedes) por aquí, la sala está al fondo.
questions.explanation: Ustedes imperative from the irregular yo-stem vengo: vengan.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Wait here, please, and be patient.'
questions.explanation: Espere and tenga are both usted imperatives built from the yo-stem.

activities.title: En la consulta
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Use formal usted imperatives in a professional setting, telling a patient what to do.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Buenos días, pase, por favor.
lines.en: Good morning, come in, please.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Gracias, buenos días.
lines.en: Thank you, good morning.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Hable despacio y explique qué le pasa.
lines.en: Speak slowly and explain what's wrong.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Estoy enfermo y muy cansado.
lines.en: I'm ill and very tired.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tome esta pastilla y descanse un poco.
lines.en: Take this pill and rest a little.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: De acuerdo, gracias.
lines.en: All right, thank you.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vuelva la semana que viene si no mejora.
lines.en: Come back next week if you don't improve.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Muy bien, muchas gracias.
lines.en: Very well, thank you very much.

days.title: Los pronombres con el imperativo: cómpralo, dímelo
days.objective: The learner can attach direct, indirect and reflexive pronouns to the affirmative imperative and add the written accent that keeps the original stress in place.
days.paretoFocus: This accent rule is tested constantly in writing and is the real difficulty of the imperative, not the verb forms themselves.
drills: Attach 'lo' to compra, toma and pon, and write the correct form of each.
Explain out loud why cómpralo needs an accent but tenlo does not.
Translate: 'Sit down here and buy it if you like it.'

items: Recall the direct object pronoun placement rule with an infinitive, from lesson 53.
Give the tú imperative of dar and decir, from lesson 78.
What is the vosotros reflexive imperative of levantarse?

activities.title: Se pega el pronombre, se marca el acento
activities.intro: When a pronoun attaches to the end of an affirmative imperative, Spanish spelling adds a written accent whenever the extra syllable would otherwise shift the stress away from where it already was.

items.hr: Cómpralo si te gusta.
items.en: Buy it if you like it.
items.note: compra + lo = cómpralo; 'compra' already stresses the first syllable, so an accent is added to keep the stress there once 'lo' adds a syllable

items.hr: Dámelo, por favor.
items.en: Give it to me, please.
items.note: da + me + lo = dámelo; two pronouns can attach, indirect before direct, and the accent again protects the original stress

items.hr: Siéntate aquí.
items.en: Sit down here.
items.note: sienta (from sentarse) + te = siéntate; reflexive pronouns attach the same way, and the accent stays on the stressed syllable

items.hr: Levantaos, ya es tarde.
items.en: Get up, it's already late.
items.note: levantad (vosotros) + os drops the -d: levantaos; no accent is needed here because the stress already falls on the right syllable

items.hr: Dímelo todo.
items.en: Tell me everything.
items.note: di + me + lo = dímelo, the same accent rule as dámelo, this time on decir's short irregular imperative

activities.title: El acento del pronombre
activities.intro: Bolt a pronoun onto each command form and decide whether it now needs a written accent.

questions.prompt: ¿Por qué lleva acento 'cómpralo'?
options: porque con el pronombre la palabra se vuelve esdrújula, y las esdrújulas siempre llevan tilde
porque todos los imperativos llevan acento
questions.answer: porque con el pronombre la palabra se vuelve esdrújula, y las esdrújulas siempre llevan tilde
questions.explanation: The stress stays on COM-, but with 'lo' attached that syllable is now third from the end, and esdrújulas always carry a written accent, the rule from the early stress lessons.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma correcta de 'give it to me' con 'dar'?
questions.explanation: Da + me + lo = dámelo, with the accent protecting the original stress on 'da'.

questions.prompt: Completa: ___ (comprar, tú) + lo, si de verdad lo necesitas.
questions.explanation: Compra + lo needs an accent to keep the stress on the original syllable: cómpralo.

questions.prompt: Completa: ¡___ (sentarse, vosotros), la película empieza ya!
questions.explanation: Sentad drops the -d before -os: sentaos, and no accent is needed because the stress already lands correctly.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Tell me the truth once and for all.'
questions.explanation: Dime = di + me, the irregular tú imperative of decir with an attached pronoun that needs no accent because the stress already falls correctly.

activities.title: Préstamelo
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Practise offering and requesting things with pronouns attached to the imperative.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Te gusta esta camiseta?
lines.en: Do you like this t-shirt?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, cómprala si te gusta tanto.
lines.en: Yes, buy it if you like it so much.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Me prestas tu diccionario?
lines.en: Will you lend me your dictionary?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Toma, tómalo, no lo necesito hoy.
lines.en: Here, take it, I don't need it today.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Estoy cansada, ¿dónde me siento?
lines.en: I'm tired, where do I sit?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Siéntate aquí, este sofá es muy cómodo.
lines.en: Sit here, this sofa is very comfortable.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¡Va a empezar la película, todos a sus sitios!
lines.en: The movie is about to start, everyone to your seats!

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: ¡Vale, levantaos y sentaos ya, chicos!
lines.en: Okay, get up and sit down now, guys!

days.title: Cómo dar indicaciones en la calle
days.objective: The learner can give and follow basic street directions using the tú imperative.
days.paretoFocus: Giving directions is a transactional task the A2 speaking prueba tests directly, and it is one of the few situations where getting the imperative wrong stops the exchange dead.
drills: Give directions from your home to the nearest shop using three imperatives.
Translate a set of directions someone gives you into English.
Translate: 'Go down this street and turn left.'

items: Give the tú imperative of ir and ser, from lesson 78.
Recall the ordinary peninsular verb for 'to take a street or bus'.
What word order do question words like dónde and cómo follow, from lesson 24?

activities.title: Sigue, gira, cruza
activities.intro: Street directions use the tú imperative of a small set of everyday verbs, some regular and one boot-changing.

items.hr: Sigue todo recto.
items.en: Keep going straight ahead.
items.note: seguir (e>i boot) tú imperative: sigue

items.hr: Gira a la derecha en el semáforo.
items.en: Turn right at the traffic light.
items.note: girar -> gira, regular

items.hr: Cruza la plaza, la parada de autobús está justo ahí.
items.en: Cross the square, the bus stop is right there.
items.note: cruzar -> cruza, regular

items.hr: Coge la segunda calle a la izquierda.
items.en: Take the second street on the left.
items.note: coger -> coge, the ordinary peninsular verb for 'to take'

items.hr: Baja por esta calle hasta el final.
items.en: Go down this street to the end.
items.note: bajar -> baja, regular

activities.title: Indicaciones en la calle
activities.intro: Practise giving street directions with the tú imperative.

questions.prompt: ¿Cómo se dice 'turn left' (tú)?
questions.explanation: Girar is regular: tú imperative gira.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es el imperativo de 'tú' para 'seguir'?
questions.explanation: Seguir is an e>i boot verb: tú imperative sigue.

questions.prompt: Completa: ___ (cruzar, tú) el puente y ya estás en el centro.
questions.explanation: Cruzar is regular: tú imperative cruza.

questions.prompt: Completa: ___ (coger, tú) la primera calle a la derecha.
questions.explanation: Coger is regular: tú imperative coge.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Go down this street and turn left.'
questions.explanation: Baja and gira are both regular tú imperatives in sequence.

activities.title: ¿Dónde está la biblioteca?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Give someone directions to the library, exercising sigue, gira, cruza and coge.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Perdona, ¿sabes dónde está la biblioteca?
lines.en: Excuse me, do you know where the library is?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, sigue todo recto hasta la plaza.
lines.en: Yes, keep going straight ahead to the square.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y luego?
lines.en: And then?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Luego gira a la derecha y cruza el parque.
lines.en: Then turn right and cross the park.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Está muy lejos?
lines.en: Is it very far?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, coge la segunda calle a la izquierda y ya la ves.
lines.en: No, take the second street on the left and you'll see it right there.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Perfecto, muchas gracias.
lines.en: Perfect, thank you very much.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: De nada, si te pierdes, pregunta otra vez, está muy cerca.
lines.en: You're welcome, if you get lost, ask again, it's very close.

days.title: Instrucciones y una receta
days.objective: The learner can write and follow a set of instructions using the imperative or the impersonal infinitive as an equivalent style.
days.paretoFocus: Recipes and manuals are a standard A2 reading genre and typically alternate between these two impersonal styles.
drills: Rewrite three imperative recipe steps in the infinitive style.
Write a short five-step recipe using either style.
Translate: 'Heat the water and add the pasta.'

items: Give the tú imperative of an o>ue boot verb, from lesson 33's family.
Recall the e>i boot change from lesson 34, applied to servir.
What does the vosotros imperative of comer look like?

activities.title: Cortar / corta la cebolla
activities.intro: Written instructions in Spanish commonly use either the tú imperative or the plain infinitive; both mean the same thing, and the infinitive style is especially common in numbered recipes and manuals.

items.hr: Corta la cebolla en trozos pequeños.
items.en: Cut the onion into small pieces.
items.note: imperative style, addressed to 'tú'

items.hr: Cortar la cebolla en trozos pequeños.
items.en: Cut the onion into small pieces.
items.note: infinitive style, impersonal, very common in written recipes and manuals, means exactly the same thing

items.hr: Añade sal y un poco de aceite.
items.en: Add salt and a bit of oil.
items.note: añadir -> añade

items.hr: Calentar el horno a doscientos grados.
items.en: Heat the oven to two hundred degrees.
items.note: the infinitive style again, typical of a numbered instruction list

items.hr: Remueve la mezcla durante dos minutos y sirve caliente.
items.en: Stir the mixture for two minutes and serve hot.
items.note: remover -> remueve (o>ue boot verb); servir -> sirve (e>i boot verb)

activities.title: Dos estilos, un significado
activities.intro: Practise the imperative and infinitive styles used in written instructions.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué estilo es habitual en una receta escrita?
questions.explanation: Written recipes and manuals very commonly use the plain infinitive as an impersonal instruction.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma equivalente de 'Añade la sal' en estilo infinitivo?
questions.explanation: The infinitive style simply uses the bare infinitive form: añadir.

questions.prompt: Completa: ___ (to cut, infinitivo) el pan en rebanadas finas.
questions.explanation: The infinitive style uses the bare infinitive as the instruction.

questions.prompt: Completa: ___ (remover, tú) la sopa antes de servirla.
questions.explanation: Remover is an o>ue boot verb: tú imperative remueve.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Heat the water and add the pasta.'
questions.explanation: Calienta and añade are both regular tú imperatives.

activities.title: La receta de la tortilla
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Explain a recipe step by step, exercising tú imperatives, boot changes and pronoun attachment.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Me explicas cómo preparas la tortilla?
lines.en: Can you explain to me how you make tortilla?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro, primero pela y corta las patatas.
lines.en: Sure, first peel and cut the potatoes.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y después?
lines.en: And after that?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Después fríelas despacio con un poco de aceite.
lines.en: After that fry them slowly with a bit of oil.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cuándo añado el huevo?
lines.en: When do I add the egg?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Bate los huevos y mézclalos con las patatas.
lines.en: Beat the eggs and mix them with the potatoes.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cuánto tiempo la cocino?
lines.en: How long do I cook it for?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Cocina la mezcla unos cinco minutos por cada lado, y sirve caliente.
lines.en: Cook the mixture about five minutes on each side, and serve hot.

days.title: Comparativos: más que, menos que, tan como
days.objective: The learner can compare people, things and actions using más...que, menos...que and tan...como, plus tanto/a/os/as como for nouns.
days.paretoFocus: Comparison is constant in everyday opinions and descriptions and appears throughout the exam's speaking and writing tasks.
drills: Compare two cities you know using más...que and menos...que.
Write one sentence with tan...como and one with tanto como.
Translate: 'I have less money than my brother.'

items: Give the imperfecto of estar in the yo form.
Recall one connector from lesson 75 used to sequence a story.
Give the usted imperative of tener, from lesson 79.

activities.title: Más que, menos que, tan como
activities.intro: Comparisons of superiority and inferiority use más or menos plus que; equality uses tan plus como with adjectives and adverbs, and tanto/a/os/as plus como when comparing nouns, agreeing in gender and number.

items.hr: Madrid es más grande que Toledo.
items.en: Madrid is bigger than Toledo.
items.note: más + adjective + que, comparative of superiority

items.hr: Este piso es menos caro que el otro.
items.en: This flat is less expensive than the other one.
items.note: menos + adjective + que, comparative of inferiority

items.hr: Mi hermano es tan alto como mi padre.
items.en: My brother is as tall as my father.
items.note: tan + adjective + como, comparative of equality

items.hr: Aquí llueve tanto como en el norte.
items.en: Here it rains as much as in the north.
items.note: tanto como with a verb, invariable

items.hr: Tengo tantos libros como tú.
items.en: I have as many books as you.
items.note: tanto/a/os/as + noun + como agrees in gender and number with the noun: tantos libros, tantas sillas

activities.title: Comparar personas y cosas
activities.intro: Practise the three comparative patterns: superiority, inferiority and equality.

questions.prompt: ¿Cómo se dice 'as expensive as' en español?
questions.explanation: Equality with an adjective uses tan + adjective + como.

questions.prompt: Elige la opción correcta: 'Tengo ___ tiempo libre ___ tú.'
questions.explanation: With a noun, tiempo, use tanto/a/os/as, agreeing in gender and number.

questions.prompt: Completa: Este examen es tan difícil ___ el anterior.
questions.explanation: Equality with an adjective: tan difícil como.

questions.prompt: Completa: Ella tiene ___ paciencia como su madre.
questions.explanation: Tanto agrees with the noun paciencia, feminine singular: tanta.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I have less money than my brother.'
questions.explanation: Comparative of inferiority: menos + noun + que.

activities.title: Madrid o Toledo
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Compare cities, neighbourhoods and daily life using all three comparative patterns.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué ciudad te gusta más, Madrid o Toledo?
lines.en: Which city do you like more, Madrid or Toledo?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Madrid es más grande que Toledo, pero Toledo es tan bonita como Madrid.
lines.en: Madrid is bigger than Toledo, but Toledo is as pretty as Madrid.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Vive mucha gente en tu barrio?
lines.en: Do a lot of people live in your neighbourhood?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No mucha, hay menos gente aquí que en el centro.
lines.en: Not many, there are fewer people here than downtown.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Trabajas tanto como antes?
lines.en: Do you work as much as before?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Trabajo tanto como el año pasado, la verdad, no ha cambiado nada.
lines.en: I work as much as last year, honestly, nothing has changed.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Tienes tantos amigos aquí como en tu ciudad?
lines.en: Do you have as many friends here as in your city?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Casi, tengo tantas amigas aquí como allí.
lines.en: Almost, I have as many friends here as there.

days.title: Los comparativos irregulares
days.objective: The learner can compare people and things using the irregular comparative forms mejor, peor, mayor and menor instead of the regular pattern.
days.paretoFocus: These four irregular comparatives are extremely frequent in everyday Spanish, and mixing up mayor/menor (age, abstract magnitude) with the standard más grande/más pequeño (physical size) is one of the clearest signs of a non-native speaker.
drills: Write three sentences comparing two people you know using mejor or peor.
Say aloud which sibling or cousin is mayor and which is menor.
Translate five English sentences with better, worse, older and younger.

items: Recall how tan como works with adjectives.
Recall how tanto/a/os/as como agrees with a noun.
Recall the difference between más...que and menos...que.

activities.title: Los comparativos irregulares
activities.intro: Bueno and malo do not form their comparative with más; they have their own short irregular forms, mejor and peor, which work for both people and things. Mayor and menor are used for age (people) and abstract magnitude, but for physical size the standard comparatives are the regular forms más grande and más pequeño. All four irregular forms add -es for the plural.

items.hr: Este hotel es mejor que el otro.
items.en: This hotel is better than the other one.
items.note: mejor = better, not más bueno

items.hr: La comida de aquí es peor que la de tu casa.
items.en: The food here is worse than at your house.
items.note: peor = worse

items.hr: Mi hermano mayor tiene treinta años.
items.en: My older brother is thirty years old.
items.note: mayor = older, referring to age

items.hr: Mi prima menor todavía va al colegio.
items.en: My younger cousin still goes to school.
items.note: menor = younger

items.hr: Estos zapatos son mejores que esos, pero son más caros.
items.en: These shoes are better than those, but they are more expensive.
items.note: mejor/peor add -es for the plural: mejores, peores

activities.title: Practica: mejor, peor, mayor, menor
activities.intro: Fill in mejor, peor, mayor or menor wherever más + adjective would sound wrong.

questions.prompt: Ese restaurante es bueno, pero el nuevo restaurante del centro es ___.
questions.explanation: Bueno has the irregular comparative mejor; más bueno is not the natural way to compare quality in Spanish.

questions.prompt: Tienes que terminar los deberes. ¿Cuál frase con el pronombre es correcta?
questions.explanation: With a periphrasis like tener que + infinitive, the pronoun can go before the conjugated verb or attach to the infinitive, but it can never split que from the infinitive.

questions.prompt: Juan tiene cuarenta años y Pedro tiene treinta. Pedro es _____ que Juan.
questions.explanation: Menor is the irregular comparative used for age: younger.

questions.prompt: Esta película es mala. La otra fue todavía _____.
questions.explanation: Peor is the irregular comparative of malo: worse.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'This shop is better than that one.'
questions.explanation: Mejor replaces más buena as the comparative of bueno; que introduces the second term of comparison.

activities.title: Comparando dos restaurantes
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends argue over which restaurant wins on food, price and service, using the four irregular comparatives.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué restaurante prefieres, este o el italiano de la esquina?
lines.en: Which restaurant do you prefer, this one or the Italian one on the corner?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: El italiano es mejor, creo.
lines.en: The Italian one is better, I think.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Mejor? A mí me parece peor, la comida es más cara.
lines.en: Better? To me it seems worse, the food is more expensive.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, pero el servicio es mucho mejor que aquí.
lines.en: Yes, but the service is much better than here.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Mi hermano mayor trabaja allí los fines de semana.
lines.en: My older brother works there on weekends.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: ¿En serio? Entonces puedes pedir por mí la próxima vez.
lines.en: Really? Then you can order for me next time.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vale, pero ese restaurante no es tan bueno como la comida de mi madre.
lines.en: Okay, but that restaurant isn't as good as my mother's food.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tienes razón, la comida de casa siempre es mejor.
lines.en: You're right, home food is always better.

days.title: El superlativo
days.objective: The learner can express 'the most' with el/la más...de and the absolute superlative with -ísimo.
days.paretoFocus: Superlatives let learners give strong opinions and vivid descriptions, both constantly needed in speaking and writing tasks.
drills: Describe the biggest city, the best restaurant and the tallest building you know using superlatives.
Turn three muy + adjective phrases into the -ísimo form.
Practise el/la más...de with three categories: food, cities, films.

items: Recall the four irregular comparatives from the previous lesson.
Recall an example sentence with mayor referring to age.
Recall how mejor and peor change in the plural.

activities.title: El superlativo
activities.intro: The superlative uses el/la/los/las + más (or menos) + adjective + de to say 'the most... in/of' a group. The absolute superlative -ísimo intensifies an adjective without comparing it to anything, and can replace muy + adjective.

items.hr: Madrid es la ciudad más grande de España.
items.en: Madrid is the biggest city in Spain.
items.note: el/la más + adjective + de = the most... in

items.hr: Este es el edificio más alto de la ciudad.
items.en: This is the tallest building in the city.

items.hr: Mi madre es la persona más simpática de mi familia.
items.en: My mother is the nicest person in my family.

items.hr: Esta tarta está riquísima.
