items.en: This cake is really delicious.
items.note: rico -> riquísimo: c changes to qu before í

items.hr: El examen fue facilísimo.
items.en: The exam was really easy.
items.note: fácil -> facilísimo: the written accent moves because the stress moves

activities.title: Practica el superlativo
activities.intro: Practice the el/la más...de pattern and the absolute superlative -ísimo.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma correcta para 'the tallest mountain in Spain'?
options: la montaña más alta de España
la montaña más alta que España
la montaña alta más de España
la más montaña alta de España
questions.answer: la montaña más alta de España
questions.explanation: The superlative pattern is el/la + noun + más + adjective + de + the group compared.

questions.prompt: Le dices a tu amigo que compre ese libro, usando el pronombre. ¿Cuál frase es correcta?
questions.explanation: The pronoun attaches to the end of the affirmative tú imperative, and a written accent is added to keep the original stress: cómpralo.

questions.prompt: Transforma 'muy fácil' en superlativo absoluto: el examen fue _____.
questions.explanation: Muy fácil intensifies to facilísimo, the absolute superlative.

questions.prompt: Este restaurante es el _____ caro de la ciudad.
questions.explanation: El + más + adjective + de forms the superlative.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'This is the most interesting museum in the city.'
questions.explanation: Superlative word order: article + noun + más + adjective + de + place.

activities.title: El mejor museo de la ciudad
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends decide which museum to visit, using superlatives.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué museo recomiendas? Quiero ver el más interesante.
lines.en: Which museum do you recommend? I want to see the most interesting one.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: El de arte moderno es facilísimo de visitar, está en el centro.
lines.en: The modern art one is really easy to visit, it's in the centre.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Es el más grande de la ciudad?
lines.en: Is it the biggest one in the city?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, el más grande es el de historia, pero el de arte moderno es el más bonito.
lines.en: No, the biggest is the history one, but the modern art one is the prettiest.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Entonces vamos al de arte moderno. Dicen que el café de dentro está riquísimo.
lines.en: Then let's go to the modern art one. They say the cafe inside is really delicious.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: ¡Perfecto! Y las entradas allí son las más baratas de toda la ciudad.
lines.en: Perfect! And the tickets there are the cheapest in the whole city.

days.title: Los adverbios en -mente
days.objective: The learner can form and use -mente adverbs, including joining two of them correctly.
days.paretoFocus: -mente adverbs let learners modify verbs precisely and appear constantly in descriptions, instructions and narration.
drills: Write three sentences using -mente adverbs formed from adjectives you already know.
Say aloud how you do three daily activities, using an adverb each time.
Join two adjectives into one -mente phrase, like clara y lentamente.

items: Recall the irregular comparatives mejor, peor, mayor and menor.
Recall how el/la más...de forms the superlative.
Recall how -ísimo intensifies an adjective.

activities.title: Los adverbios en -mente
activities.intro: Adverbs of manner are formed by adding -mente to the feminine singular form of the adjective; adjectives with a single form for both genders just add -mente directly. When two -mente adverbs are joined by y, only the second one keeps the suffix.

items.hr: Habla muy lentamente.
items.en: He speaks very slowly.
items.note: lento -> lenta -> lentamente

items.hr: Normalmente ceno a las nueve.
items.en: I usually have dinner at nine.
items.note: normal has one form for both genders, so it just adds -mente

items.hr: Ella conduce rápidamente por la autopista.
items.en: She drives fast on the motorway.

items.hr: Lo hizo clara y tranquilamente.
items.en: She did it clearly and calmly.
items.note: when two -mente adverbs are joined, the first drops -mente and keeps only the feminine adjective

items.hr: Últimamente trabajo mucho.
items.en: Lately I work a lot.

activities.title: Practica los adverbios en -mente
activities.intro: Practice forming and joining -mente adverbs.

questions.prompt: ¿Cómo se forma el adverbio a partir de 'feliz'?
questions.explanation: Adjectives with a single form for both genders, like feliz, add -mente directly.

questions.prompt: Elige la frase correcta para 'She spoke slowly and clearly.'
questions.explanation: When two -mente adverbs are joined by y, only the second keeps -mente; the first stays as the feminine adjective.

questions.prompt: Ana siempre llega tarde, pero hoy llegó _____.
questions.explanation: Puntual -> puntualmente: adjectives ending in a consonant just add -mente.

questions.prompt: Mi abuela cocina muy bien; prepara la comida _____.
questions.explanation: Perfecto -> perfecta -> perfectamente.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'She explained it very clearly and slowly.'
questions.explanation: Muy modifies the whole pair; the first adverb, clara, drops -mente, and the second, lentamente, keeps it.

activities.title: Cómo lo hago
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends talk about how they cook, using -mente adverbs.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cómo preparas la tortilla, rápidamente o con calma?
lines.en: How do you make the tortilla, quickly or calmly?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Normalmente la hago lentamente, así queda perfecta.
lines.en: I usually make it slowly, that way it turns out perfect.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Yo, en cambio, cocino rápidamente porque tengo poco tiempo.
lines.en: I, on the other hand, cook quickly because I have little time.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Últimamente cocino mucho, pero como muy mal.
lines.en: Lately I cook a lot, but I eat very badly.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tienes que cocinar más tranquilamente y no tan deprisa.
lines.en: You have to cook more calmly and not so fast.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tienes razón, voy a intentarlo la próxima vez.
lines.en: You're right, I'm going to try it next time.

days.title: Muy o mucho
days.objective: The learner can choose correctly between muy and mucho in every context.
days.paretoFocus: English speakers get this wrong more persistently than almost anything else in Spanish, and because muy and mucho attach to different word classes, fixing it lifts accuracy across every topic at once.
drills: Write five sentences alternating muy and mucho correctly.
Describe your week using mucho with a verb and mucho/mucha with a noun.
Correct three sentences that mix up muy and mucho.

items: Recall how -mente adverbs are formed.
Recall the rule for joining two -mente adverbs with y.
Recall the superlative pattern el/la más...de.

activities.title: Muy o mucho
activities.intro: Muy modifies an adjective or an adverb and can never stand alone. Mucho modifies a verb, staying invariable, or a noun, in which case it agrees in gender and number: mucho, mucha, muchos, muchas.

items.hr: Este libro es muy interesante.
items.en: This book is very interesting.
items.note: muy + adjective

items.hr: Hablas muy bien español.
items.en: You speak Spanish very well.
items.note: muy + adverb (bien)

items.hr: Trabajo mucho los lunes.
items.en: I work a lot on Mondays.
items.note: mucho modifying a verb stays invariable

items.hr: Tengo mucha hambre.
items.en: I am very hungry.
items.note: mucho agrees with a feminine noun: mucha hambre

items.hr: Hay muchos coches en esta calle.
items.en: There are many cars on this street.
items.note: mucho agrees with a plural masculine noun: muchos

activities.title: Practica muy y mucho
activities.intro: Practice choosing between muy and mucho.

questions.prompt: Elige la opción correcta: 'Estoy ___ cansado hoy.'
questions.explanation: Muy modifies the adjective cansado; mucho cannot modify an adjective directly.

questions.prompt: Elige la opción correcta: 'Duermo ___ los fines de semana.'
questions.explanation: Mucho modifies the verb dormir here and stays invariable.

questions.prompt: Tenemos _____ amigos en esta ciudad.
questions.explanation: Mucho agrees with the plural masculine noun amigos: muchos.

questions.prompt: En una receta, la instrucción impersonal para 'cut the onion' es: _____ la cebolla.
questions.explanation: Recipes often use the bare infinitive as an impersonal instruction instead of the imperative.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I sleep very little, but I work a lot.'
questions.explanation: Poco is modified by muy (adverb use); trabajo is modified by mucho (verb use).

activities.title: Muy cansado, pero contento
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend asks about a long trip, using muy and mucho.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Estás muy cansado después del viaje?
lines.en: Are you very tired after the trip?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, estoy muy cansado, pero muy contento.
lines.en: Yes, I'm very tired, but very happy.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Comiste mucho por el camino?
lines.en: Did you eat a lot on the way?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No mucho, pero bebí muchísima agua.
lines.en: Not much, but I drank a huge amount of water.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tienes mucha suerte, ya has llegado.
lines.en: You're very lucky, you've already arrived.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es verdad, y ahora solo quiero descansar mucho.
lines.en: That's true, and now I just want to rest a lot.

days.title: Los posesivos tónicos
days.objective: The learner can use the stressed possessives mío, tuyo, suyo, nuestro and vuestro to say what belongs to whom.
days.paretoFocus: Stressed possessives are needed to answer 'whose is this' and to say 'a friend of mine', both extremely common in daily conversation.
drills: Write five sentences saying an object is mío, tuyo, suyo or nuestro.
Describe three things that belong to a friend using an amigo mío style phrase.
Practise the contrast between mi coche and el coche es mío.

items: Recall the difference between muy and mucho.
Recall an example of a two-adverb -mente phrase.
Recall the irregular comparative for bueno.

activities.title: Los posesivos tónicos
activities.intro: This second set of possessives changes its ending to match the thing owned, not the owner, and sits after the noun or stands alone after ser: es mío, la casa es nuestra. The short forms mi, tu and su that you already know always come before the noun instead.

items.hr: Este bolso es mío.
items.en: This bag is mine.

items.hr: ¿Es tuya esta chaqueta?
items.en: Is this jacket yours?

items.hr: Un amigo mío vive en Bilbao.
items.en: A friend of mine lives in Bilbao.
items.note: amigo mío: the stressed possessive goes after the noun

items.hr: La casa es nuestra, no es vuestra.
items.en: The house is ours, it isn't yours (plural).

items.hr: Estas llaves no son suyas, son mías.
items.en: These keys aren't his, hers or theirs, they're mine.
items.note: suyo covers his, hers, formal yours and theirs; context clarifies which

activities.title: Practica los posesivos tónicos
activities.intro: Pick the possessive that agrees with the object owned rather than with the owner.

questions.prompt: ¿Cómo se dice 'This is not my problem, it's yours' a un amigo?
options: Este no es mi problema, es tuyo.
Este no es mi problema, es tuya.
Este no es mío problema, es tuyo.
Este no es mi problema, es tu.
questions.answer: Este no es mi problema, es tuyo.
questions.explanation: Tuyo stands alone after ser and agrees with problema (masculine): tuyo.

questions.prompt: Elige la traducción correcta de 'This flat is as big as that one.'
options: Este piso es tan grande como ese.
Este piso es más grande tan ese.
Este piso es tan grande que ese.
Este piso es igual grande como ese.
questions.answer: Este piso es tan grande como ese.
questions.explanation: Tan + adjective + como is the equality comparative.

questions.prompt: Esta maleta es de Pedro. Esta maleta es _____.
questions.explanation: Suyo/a agrees with maleta (feminine) and refers back to Pedro: suya.

questions.prompt: Ana y yo compramos esta casa juntos. La casa es _____.
questions.explanation: Nuestra agrees with casa (feminine) and shows shared possession.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'A friend of mine works with your brother.'
questions.explanation: Amigo mío places the stressed possessive after the noun; tu hermano keeps the unstressed possessive before the noun.

activities.title: ¿De quién es esto?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends sort out lost items, using stressed possessives.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿De quién es este paraguas? ¿Es tuyo?
lines.en: Whose umbrella is this? Is it yours?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, no es mío. Creo que es de Laura.
lines.en: No, it's not mine. I think it's Laura's.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y esta bufanda? Parece tuya.
lines.en: And this scarf? It looks like yours.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: ¡Ah, sí, es mía! Gracias.
lines.en: Oh yes, it's mine! Thanks.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Un compañero mío perdió unas llaves aquí la semana pasada.
lines.en: A colleague of mine lost some keys here last week.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: ¿Son estas llaves? Seguramente son suyas.
lines.en: Are these the keys? They're probably his.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Sí, esas son. Voy a llamarlo ahora mismo.
lines.en: Yes, those are them. I'm going to call him right now.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Perfecto, así recupera lo suyo.
lines.en: Perfect, that way he gets his things back.

days.title: El relativo que
days.objective: The learner can join two ideas about a person or thing using the restrictive relative que.
days.paretoFocus: Relative que lets learners give more precise, natural descriptions instead of two short disconnected sentences.
drills: Write five sentences describing people or things using que.
Combine two short sentences into one using que.
Practise saying que without a written accent aloud, contrasted with qué.

items: Recall how to say something belongs to you using a stressed possessive.
Recall the plural of mío, tuyo and suyo.
Recall un amigo mío as an example phrase.

activities.title: El relativo que
activities.intro: The relative que introduces a clause that identifies exactly who or what you mean, whether the antecedent is a person or a thing. It never carries a written accent, unlike the question word qué.

items.hr: El libro que compré es muy bueno.
items.en: The book that I bought is very good.

items.hr: La chica que vive al lado es profesora.
items.en: The girl who lives next door is a teacher.

items.hr: El hombre que habla con Ana es mi jefe.
items.en: The man who is talking to Ana is my boss.

items.hr: Estos son los zapatos que quiero comprar.
items.en: These are the shoes that I want to buy.

items.hr: Tengo un amigo que vive en Portugal.
items.en: I have a friend who lives in Portugal.
items.note: que (no written accent) introduces the relative clause; qué (with accent) is only the question word

activities.title: Practica el relativo que
activities.intro: Practice restrictive relative clauses with que.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta?
options: El coche que compré es rojo.
El coche qué compré es rojo.
El coche que compre es rojo.
El coche cual compré es rojo.
questions.answer: El coche que compré es rojo.
questions.explanation: The relative que never carries a written accent, unlike the question word qué.

questions.prompt: Elige la frase con el relativo que se refiere a una persona.
options: La mujer que trabaja aquí es mi tía.
La mujer que trabajo aquí es mi tía.
La mujer que trabajan aquí es mi tía.
La mujer que trabajas aquí es mi tía.
questions.answer: La mujer que trabaja aquí es mi tía.
questions.explanation: The verb after que must agree with the person it describes: la mujer -> trabaja.

questions.prompt: Tengo una vecina _____ siempre me ayuda.
questions.explanation: Que introduces a restrictive relative clause referring to vecina.

questions.prompt: Este hotel es _____ que el otro, tiene mejores habitaciones.
questions.explanation: Mejor is the irregular comparative of bueno.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'The restaurant that we visited yesterday was excellent.'
questions.explanation: Que introduces the relative clause visitamos ayer, describing el restaurante.

activities.title: La persona que busco
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends figure out who someone is, using relative clauses with que.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Conoces a la persona que trabaja en el hospital nuevo?
lines.en: Do you know the person who works at the new hospital?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, es una amiga que conocí el año pasado.
lines.en: Yes, she's a friend that I met last year.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Es la chica que vive en tu edificio?
lines.en: Is she the girl who lives in your building?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, es la mujer que tiene el pelo largo y trabaja los fines de semana.
lines.en: No, she's the woman who has long hair and works on weekends.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ah, ya sé quién es. El café que hacen allí es buenísimo.
lines.en: Ah, now I know who she is. The coffee they make there is really good.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es verdad, y el médico que me atendió también fue muy amable.
lines.en: That's true, and the doctor who saw me was also very kind.

days.title: Indefinidos y cuantificadores
days.objective: The learner can use algo/nada, alguien/nadie, algún/ningún, todo, otro, demasiado, bastante and poco to talk about quantity and existence.
days.paretoFocus: These indefinites and quantifiers appear in almost every everyday conversation about shopping, plans and opinions.
drills: Write five sentences about a nearly empty kitchen, pairing each affirmative indefinite with its negative twin.
Describe a nearly empty fridge using nada and poco.
Practise the double negative pattern with no...nadie.

items: Recall a sentence using the relative que.
Recall the difference between qué and que.
Recall how to combine two sentences with que.

activities.title: Indefinidos y cuantificadores
activities.intro: Nadie answers alguien and nada answers algo, the same way ningún answers algún: every affirmative indefinite in Spanish has a negative counterpart. Before a masculine singular noun, algún and ningún drop the final -o, and a negative sentence still needs no before the verb even with nadie or nada already in it.

items.hr: ¿Hay algo de comer? No, no hay nada.
items.en: Is there something to eat? No, there's nothing.

items.hr: ¿Conoces a alguien aquí? No, no conozco a nadie.
items.en: Do you know anyone here? No, I don't know anyone.

items.hr: No tengo ningún problema con eso.
items.en: I don't have any problem with that.
items.note: algún/ningún drop the final -o before a masculine singular noun

items.hr: Ya he leído todo el libro.
items.en: I've already read the whole book.

items.hr: Hay demasiada gente y poco espacio aquí.
items.en: There are too many people and too little space here.

activities.title: Practica los indefinidos
activities.intro: Practice choosing indefinites and quantifiers.

questions.prompt: Elige la opción correcta: 'No hay ___ leche en la nevera.'
questions.explanation: Nada de + uncountable noun expresses 'no... at all': no hay nada de leche.

questions.prompt: Elige la opción correcta: '¿Tienes ___ duda sobre el examen?'
questions.explanation: Algún shortens before a masculine singular noun; before a feminine noun like duda, the full form alguna is used.

questions.prompt: No conozco a _____ en esta fiesta, no tengo amigos aquí.
questions.explanation: Nadie is the negative counterpart of alguien and needs no before the verb.

questions.prompt: Este es el plato _____ picante de todo el menú.
questions.explanation: El + más + adjective + de forms the superlative.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'There's too much noise and too little space here.'
questions.explanation: Demasiado and poco both agree with the noun they quantify; here both are masculine singular nouns, ruido and espacio.

activities.title: No hay nada que hacer
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends plan a quiet evening, using indefinites.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Hay algo interesante en la tele esta noche?
lines.en: Is there anything interesting on TV tonight?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, no hay nada que hacer, todo es aburrido.
lines.en: No, there's nothing to do, everything is boring.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Alguien te ha llamado hoy?
lines.en: Has anyone called you today?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, nadie me ha llamado, y no tengo ningún plan para esta noche.
lines.en: No, nobody has called me, and I don't have any plan for tonight.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Pues tengo algunas ideas: podemos ver una película o salir a caminar.
lines.en: Well, I have a few ideas: we can watch a movie or go for a walk.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, las dos opciones me parecen bien.
lines.en: Okay, both options seem fine to me.

days.title: Cuando + presente: la costumbre
days.objective: The learner can describe habitual situations with cuando + present indicative.
days.paretoFocus: Routines and habitual cause-and-effect are what a learner at this level actually needs to talk about, and getting the tense right here also avoids preempting the future use of cuando that arrives with the subjunctive.
drills: Write five sentences describing your habits using cuando + present.
Describe what a family member always does when it rains.
Practise three cuando sentences about your weekly routine.

items: Recall three indefinite words and their negative counterparts.
Recall how algún and ningún change before a masculine singular noun.
Recall an example with demasiado or poco.

activities.title: Cuando + presente
activities.intro: Cuando + present indicative describes something that happens every time a condition is met, a habit or a general truth. Using cuando for one specific future event needs a different form that this course teaches later, so for now this pattern only covers habits and routines.

items.hr: Cuando llueve, cojo el paraguas.
items.en: When it rains, I take the umbrella.
items.note: habitual: every time it rains

items.hr: Cuando viene mi hermano, trae regalos.
items.en: When my brother comes, he brings gifts.

items.hr: Cuando tengo tiempo libre, leo novelas.
items.en: When I have free time, I read novels.

items.hr: Cuando estamos cansados, nos acostamos pronto.
items.en: When we're tired, we go to bed early.

items.hr: Cuando hace frío, mi madre siempre pone la calefacción.
items.en: When it's cold, my mother always turns on the heating.

activities.title: Practica cuando + presente
activities.intro: Practice cuando + present for habitual situations.

questions.prompt: Elige la frase que expresa una costumbre.
options: Cuando llego a casa, ceno enseguida.
Cuando llegué a casa, cené enseguida.
Cuando he llegado a casa, he cenado enseguida.
Cuando estoy llegando a casa, ceno enseguida.
questions.answer: Cuando llego a casa, ceno enseguida.
questions.explanation: Only the present indicative in both halves gives the habitual reading, every time I get home. The indefinido and the perfecto both report one particular occasion, and estar + gerundio describes a moment in progress rather than a routine.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué significa 'Cuando viajo, siempre saco fotos'?
options: A general habit every time I travel
A single planned trip next month
A story about a past trip
questions.answer: A general habit every time I travel
questions.explanation: Cuando + present here signals a repeated habitual pattern, not a single event.

questions.prompt: Cuando _____ prisa, no desayuno.
questions.explanation: Tener conjugates in the present indicative for the habitual cuando clause: tengo.

questions.prompt: Mi padre conduce muy _____ cuando lleva a los niños al colegio.
questions.explanation: Lento -> lentamente, an -mente adverb.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'When I'm on holiday, I always sleep late.'
questions.explanation: Cuando + present expresses the habitual pattern: every time I'm on holiday.

activities.title: Cuando tengo un día libre
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends talk about their habits, using cuando + present.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué haces cuando tienes un día libre?
lines.en: What do you do when you have a day off?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Cuando tengo un día libre, duermo hasta tarde y luego salgo a pasear.
lines.en: When I have a day off, I sleep late and then go out for a walk.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y cuando hace mal tiempo?
lines.en: And when the weather is bad?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Cuando llueve, me quedo en casa y leo o veo una película.
lines.en: When it rains, I stay home and read or watch a movie.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Yo, cuando estoy libre, siempre quedo con mis amigos.
lines.en: I, when I'm free, always meet up with my friends.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Qué bien. Cuando tengo tiempo, prefiero estar tranquilo en casa.
lines.en: That's nice. When I have time, I prefer to be quiet at home.

days.title: Antes de y después de + infinitivo
days.objective: The learner can sequence two actions done by the same person using antes de and después de + infinitive.
days.paretoFocus: Sequencing daily actions is essential for describing routines and stories, and the same-subject rule prevents a very common learner error.
drills: Write five sentences about your morning routine, using antes de or después de each time.
Describe what you do before and after work using the infinitive.
Practise the same-subject rule out loud with three examples.

items: Recall a habitual sentence with cuando + present.
Recall why cuando + present cannot yet describe a single future event.
Recall an example sentence with cuando about the weather.

activities.title: Antes de y después de + infinitivo
activities.intro: When one person carries out two actions in order, Spanish links them with antes de or después de followed by an infinitive rather than a full clause. Both verbs must share the same subject; describing two different people needs a structure taught later in the course.

items.hr: Antes de salir, cierro la puerta con llave.
items.en: Before leaving, I lock the door.

items.hr: Después de comer, siempre duermo un poco.
items.en: After eating, I always sleep a little.

items.hr: Nos duchamos antes de desayunar.
items.en: We shower before having breakfast.

items.hr: Después de terminar el trabajo, voy al gimnasio.
items.en: After finishing work, I go to the gym.

items.hr: Antes de dormir, leo un rato.
items.en: Before sleeping, I read for a while.
items.note: antes de/después de + infinitive only works when the same person does both actions

activities.title: Practica antes de y después de
activities.intro: Choose whether antes de or después de fits, then supply the right infinitive after it.

questions.prompt: Elige la frase correcta para 'After working, I go home.'
options: Después de trabajar, voy a casa.
Después de trabajo, voy a casa.
Después que trabajo, voy a casa.
questions.answer: Después de trabajar, voy a casa.
questions.explanation: Después de is always followed by the infinitive when the subject stays the same.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuándo se puede usar antes de + infinitivo?
options: Cuando la misma persona hace las dos acciones
Cuando dos personas distintas hacen cada acción
questions.answer: Cuando la misma persona hace las dos acciones
questions.explanation: Antes de/después de + infinitive requires a single shared subject for both actions.

questions.prompt: _____ de vestirme, desayuno tranquilamente.
questions.explanation: Antes de + infinitive: before getting dressed.

questions.prompt: Estoy _____ cansado después de este viaje tan largo.
questions.explanation: Muy modifies the adjective cansado.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Before eating, we always wash our hands.'
questions.explanation: Antes de + infinitive comes first, then the main clause with the reflexive verb lavarse.

activities.title: La rutina de la mañana
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends compare their morning routines.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué haces antes de salir de casa?
lines.en: What do you do before leaving home?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Antes de salir, desayuno y me visto rápidamente.
lines.en: Before leaving, I have breakfast and get dressed quickly.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Te duchas antes o después de desayunar?
lines.en: Do you shower before or after having breakfast?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Me ducho antes de desayunar, así me despierto mejor.
lines.en: I shower before having breakfast, that way I wake up better.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Yo, después de ducharme, siempre tomo un café.
lines.en: I, after showering, always have a coffee.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Después de desayunar, salgo corriendo para no llegar tarde.
lines.en: After having breakfast, I rush out so I don't arrive late.

days.title: Desde, desde hace y hace... que
days.objective: The learner can express how long something has been going on using desde, desde hace and hace... que.
days.paretoFocus: Talking about duration up to the present is needed constantly in interviews, small talk and forms.
drills: Write three sentences about how long you have lived somewhere.
Practise flipping the word order between hace... que and desde hace for the same sentence.
Ask a friend desde cuándo they have known someone.

items: Recall the same-subject rule for antes de/después de + infinitive.
Recall an example sentence with después de.
Recall an example sentence combining antes de with a reflexive verb.

activities.title: Desde, desde hace, hace... que
activities.intro: Desde marks a starting point (desde 2015, desde el lunes), while hace... que and desde hace both describe a stretch of time that continues into now, paired with the present tense. Either order carries the same meaning, so pick whichever feels more natural in the sentence.

items.hr: Vivo en Madrid desde 2015.
items.en: I've lived in Madrid since 2015.

items.hr: Estudio español desde hace tres años.
items.en: I've been studying Spanish for three years.

items.hr: Hace tres años que estudio español.
items.en: It's been three years since I started studying Spanish.
items.note: same meaning as desde hace tres años, different word order

items.hr: Trabajamos aquí desde hace poco tiempo.
items.en: We've been working here for a short time.

items.hr: ¿Desde cuándo conoces a Marta? La conozco desde el año pasado.
items.en: Since when have you known Marta? I've known her since last year.

activities.title: Practica desde y hace... que
activities.intro: Choose whether desde, desde hace or hace... que best fits the gap.

questions.prompt: Elige la opción correcta para 'I've lived here for ten years.'
options: Vivo aquí desde hace diez años.
questions.answer: Vivo aquí desde hace diez años.
questions.explanation: Desde hace + a period of time expresses a duration up to now, used with the present tense.

questions.prompt: Elige la opción correcta para 'Since when do you work here?'
questions.explanation: Desde cuándo asks for the starting point of an ongoing action, so the present tense follows.

questions.prompt: _____ dos meses que no veo a mis padres.
questions.explanation: Hace + period + que + present expresses how long something has been going on.

questions.prompt: Este paraguas no es de nadie más, es totalmente _____.
questions.explanation: Mío stands alone after ser to show possession.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I've known him since I was a child.'
questions.explanation: Desde que introduces a clause meaning 'ever since'; era is the imperfecto of ser used to describe a past state.

activities.title: Desde hace mucho tiempo
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends talk about how long they have lived in the neighbourhood.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cuánto tiempo hace que vives en este barrio?
lines.en: How long have you been living in this neighbourhood?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vivo aquí desde hace ocho años.
lines.en: I've lived here for eight years.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y conoces a los vecinos desde el principio?
lines.en: And have you known the neighbours since the beginning?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A algunos sí, los conozco desde hace mucho tiempo.
lines.en: Some of them yes, I've known them for a long time.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Yo llegué hace solo un mes, todavía no conozco a nadie.
lines.en: I arrived just a month ago, I still don't know anyone.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No te preocupes, aquí la gente es muy simpática desde el primer día.
lines.en: Don't worry, people here are very nice from the first day.

days.title: Porque, como y es que
days.objective: The learner can give a reason using porque, como and es que in the right position.
days.paretoFocus: Explaining reasons is essential for justifying decisions and answering por qué questions naturally.
drills: Write three sentences giving a reason with porque.
Rewrite three of those sentences starting with como instead.
Practise answering a por qué question with es que.

items: Recall how to say you have lived somewhere for three years.
Recall the two word orders for desde hace and hace... que.
Recall how to ask desde cuándo someone has known another person.

activities.title: Porque, como, es que
activities.intro: Porque introduces a reason after the result it explains; como fronts the reason at the start of the sentence, with the result following; es que softens a spoken explanation or excuse, often as a direct answer to a question.

items.hr: No voy a la fiesta porque estoy cansado.
items.en: I'm not going to the party because I'm tired.

items.hr: Como estoy cansado, no voy a la fiesta.
items.en: Since I'm tired, I'm not going to the party.
items.note: como goes at the start of the sentence and the result follows

items.hr: ¿Por qué no vienes? Es que tengo que trabajar.
items.en: Why aren't you coming? It's just that I have to work.
items.note: es que softens an excuse

items.hr: Como hacía frío, nos quedamos en casa.
items.en: Since it was cold, we stayed home.

items.hr: Llegué tarde porque perdí el autobús.
items.en: I arrived late because I missed the bus.

activities.title: Practica porque, como y es que
activities.intro: Pick porque, como or es que and put it exactly where Spanish word order requires.

questions.prompt: Elige la posición correcta de 'como' causal.
options: Como no tenía dinero, no compré nada.
No tenía dinero, como no compré nada.
No compré nada como no tenía dinero.
Como, no tenía dinero no compré nada.
questions.answer: Como no tenía dinero, no compré nada.
questions.explanation: Causal como must open the sentence, with the result in the second clause.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la mejor respuesta a '¿Por qué no comes?'?
options: Es porque que no tengo hambre.
questions.explanation: Es que introduces a spoken, softened explanation, common as a direct answer.

questions.prompt: No salgo _____ tengo mucho trabajo.
questions.explanation: Porque introduces the cause after the main clause.

questions.prompt: Este es el vecino _____ me ayudó ayer con las bolsas.
questions.explanation: Que introduces a relative clause describing vecino.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Since it was raining, we stayed at the office.'
questions.explanation: Como fronts the cause; llovía is the imperfecto used to describe an ongoing past condition.

activities.title: ¿Por qué no viniste?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend explains why they missed a meeting, using es que, como and porque to give reasons.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Por qué no viniste a la reunión ayer?
lines.en: Why didn't you come to the meeting yesterday?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es que tuve un problema con el coche.
lines.en: It's just that I had a problem with the car.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vaya, ¿y qué pasó?
lines.en: Wow, and what happened?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Como no arrancaba, tuve que llamar a un taller.
lines.en: Since it wouldn't start, I had to call a garage.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y llegaste tarde al trabajo porque el taller tardó mucho?
lines.en: And did you arrive late to work because the garage took a long time?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, exacto, por eso no pude ir a la reunión.
lines.en: Yes, exactly, that's why I couldn't go to the meeting.

days.title: Para + infinitivo: la finalidad
days.objective: The learner can express purpose with para + infinitive.
days.paretoFocus: Saying why you do something is needed in almost every explanation, from daily plans to formal requests.
drills: Write five sentences explaining why you do something using para + infinitive.
Describe the purpose of three objects around your home.
Practise answering a para qué question.

items: Recall an example sentence using como to give a reason.
Recall how es que softens an explanation.
Recall the position of como at the start of a sentence.

activities.title: Para + infinitivo
activities.intro: Para + infinitive expresses the purpose of an action, when the same person does both things. It answers the question 'why' or 'what for.'

items.hr: Estudio mucho para aprobar el examen.
items.en: I study a lot to pass the exam.

items.hr: Voy al supermercado para comprar fruta.
items.en: I'm going to the supermarket to buy fruit.

items.hr: Llamo a mi madre para saber cómo está.
items.en: I call my mother to find out how she is.

items.hr: Necesitas una llave para abrir esta puerta.
items.en: You need a key to open this door.

items.hr: Trabajamos duro para vivir mejor.
items.en: We work hard to live better.

activities.title: Practica para + infinitivo
activities.intro: Practice expressing purpose with para + infinitive.

questions.prompt: Elige la frase correcta para 'I save money to travel.'
questions.explanation: Para + infinitive expresses the purpose of the action, when the subject is the same.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué expresa 'para' en 'Vengo para ayudarte'?
questions.explanation: Para + infinitive here answers 'why', the purpose of coming.

questions.prompt: Abro la ventana _____ ventilar la habitación.
questions.explanation: Para + infinitive: to ventilate the room.

questions.prompt: Necesito _____ información antes de decidir.
questions.explanation: Alguna agrees with the feminine noun información.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'We need a map to find the museum.'
questions.explanation: Para + infinitive expresses purpose: in order to find the museum.

activities.title: Para qué sirve esto
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends talk about study habits, using para + infinitive.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Para qué necesitas ese libro tan grande?
lines.en: What do you need that huge book for?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Lo necesito para estudiar para el examen de la próxima semana.
lines.en: I need it to study for next week's exam.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y para qué vas a la biblioteca todos los días?
lines.en: And why do you go to the library every day?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Voy para tener silencio y concentrarme mejor.
lines.en: I go to have silence and concentrate better.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Yo prefiero estudiar en casa para ahorrar tiempo.
lines.en: I prefer to study at home to save time.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Cada uno estudia para aprender a su manera.
lines.en: Everyone studies to learn in their own way.

days.title: Por o para: el primer contraste
days.objective: The learner can choose between por and para in the clearest contrast: cause and exchange versus destination and purpose.
days.paretoFocus: This first clean split prevents the single most common preposition error in Spanish before the fuller system is taught later.
drills: Write three sentences with para for a recipient or destination.
Write three sentences with por for a cause or exchange.
Practise the trabajo para ella / trabajo por ella contrast aloud.

items: Recall an example sentence with para + infinitive expressing purpose.
Recall the difference between para + infinitive and por + noun.
Recall a sentence explaining why you study.

activities.title: Por o para: el primer contraste
activities.intro: This is only the first, cleanest contrast between por and para. Para points forward, to a destination, a recipient or a purpose. Por points back, to a cause, a reason or an exchange. The fuller system comes later; for now, these paired examples make the difference concrete.

items.hr: Trabajo para ella.
items.en: I work for her.
items.note: para = she is my boss, the recipient of my work

items.hr: Trabajo por ella.
items.en: I'm covering her shift.
items.note: por = cause or substitution, doing it in her place

items.hr: Compré este regalo para ti.
items.en: I bought this gift for you.

items.hr: Pagué veinte euros por este libro.
items.en: I paid twenty euros for this book.
items.note: por = exchange, what was given in return

items.hr: Salgo para Madrid mañana.
items.en: I'm leaving for Madrid tomorrow.
items.note: para = destination

activities.title: Practica por y para
activities.intro: Practice the clean contrast between por and para.

questions.prompt: Elige 'por' o 'para': 'Este regalo es ___ mi madre, es su cumpleaños.'
questions.explanation: Para marks the recipient of the gift.

questions.prompt: Elige 'por' o 'para': 'Gracias ___ tu ayuda.'
questions.explanation: Por marks the cause or reason for the thanks.

questions.prompt: Hoy trabajo _____ mi compañero porque está enfermo.
questions.explanation: Por here means 'in his place, covering for him'.

questions.prompt: Cuando _____ mucho, siempre cojo el paraguas.
questions.explanation: Cuando + present indicative for a habitual pattern.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I bought flowers for my grandmother.'
questions.explanation: Para marks the recipient of the flowers.

activities.title: ¿Por ella o para ella?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two colleagues talk about work, using por and para.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Trabajas hoy por Marta? Pensaba que ella trabajaba los sábados.
lines.en: Are you working today for Marta? I thought she worked Saturdays.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, trabajo por ella porque está de vacaciones.
lines.en: Yes, I'm covering for her because she's on holiday.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ah, entiendo. Y este informe, ¿es para el jefe?
lines.en: Ah, I see. And this report, is it for the boss?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, lo preparo para él, lo necesita para mañana.
lines.en: Yes, I'm preparing it for him, he needs it for tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cuánto pagaste por la impresora nueva?
lines.en: How much did you pay for the new printer?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Pagué cien euros por ella, no estaba mal de precio.
lines.en: I paid a hundred euros for it, the price wasn't bad.

days.title: Saber o conocer; pedir o preguntar
days.objective: The learner can choose correctly between saber and conocer, and between pedir and preguntar.
days.paretoFocus: English collapses each of these pairs into one verb, so giving the learner a decision rule prevents a recurring, high-frequency error.
drills: Write three sentences with saber and three with conocer.
Write three sentences with pedir and three with preguntar.
Practise the personal a with conocer aloud.

items: Recall the clean contrast between por and para from the previous lesson.
Recall an example sentence with trabajo para alguien.
Recall an example with pagar por algo.

activities.title: Saber o conocer; pedir o preguntar
activities.intro: Use saber for facts, information and learned skills (saber + infinitive = to know how to); use conocer for familiarity with people, places and things, remembering the personal a before a person: conozco a tu hermano. Use pedir when you request something concrete, an object, a favour, permission; use preguntar when you ask a question or ask for information.

items.hr: Sé conducir, pero no tengo coche.
items.en: I know how to drive, but I don't have a car.
items.note: saber + infinitive = to know how to

items.hr: Conozco un restaurante muy bueno cerca de aquí.
items.en: I know a really good restaurant near here.
items.note: conocer = to be familiar with a place or thing

items.hr: Le pido un favor a mi vecino.
items.en: I'm asking my neighbour for a favour.
items.note: pedir = to ask for/request something

items.hr: Le pregunto la hora a una señora.
items.en: I ask a lady the time.
items.note: preguntar = to ask a question/for information

items.hr: No sé la respuesta, así que voy a preguntar.
items.en: I don't know the answer, so I'm going to ask.

activities.title: Practica saber, conocer, pedir, preguntar
activities.intro: Practice choosing between saber/conocer and pedir/preguntar.

questions.prompt: Elige la opción correcta: '¿___ tocar el piano?'
questions.explanation: Saber + infinitive asks about a learned skill.

questions.prompt: Elige la opción correcta: '¿___ a mi hermana? Trabaja contigo.'
questions.explanation: Conocer is used for familiarity with a person, and takes the personal a.

questions.prompt: En el restaurante, le _____ la cuenta al camarero.
questions.explanation: Pedir is used to request something concrete, here the bill.

questions.prompt: _____ de cenar, siempre lavo los platos.
questions.explanation: Después de + infinitive.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I don't know this city, but I know how to read a map.'
questions.explanation: Conocer for familiarity with the city, saber + infinitive for the skill of reading a map.

activities.title: ¿Sabes o conoces?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends look for a place to eat, using saber, conocer, pedir and preguntar.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Conoces algún restaurante bueno por aquí?
lines.en: Do you know any good restaurant around here?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, conozco uno estupendo, pero no sé si está abierto los lunes.
lines.en: Yes, I know a great one, but I don't know if it's open on Mondays.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Por qué no le preguntas al camarero de la esquina?
lines.en: Why don't you ask the waiter on the corner?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Buena idea, voy a preguntarle la dirección exacta.
lines.en: Good idea, I'm going to ask him for the exact address.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Y si está cerrado, podemos pedir una pizza en casa.
lines.en: And if it's closed, we can order a pizza at home.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, pero primero quiero saber si el otro sitio tiene mesa libre.
lines.en: Okay, but first I want to know if the other place has a free table.

days.title: La casa y alquilar un piso
days.objective: The learner can describe a flat and handle the basic vocabulary and structures needed to rent one.
days.paretoFocus: Renting a home is one of the first practical tasks a new resident faces, and the vocabulary recurs in every housing conversation.
drills: Describe your own home using habitación, salón, cocina and baño.
Write three questions you would ask before renting a flat.
Practise the phrase pagar una fianza antes de firmar el contrato.

items: Recall the difference between saber and conocer.
Recall the difference between pedir and preguntar.
Recall an example with the personal a and conocer.

activities.title: La casa y alquilar un piso
activities.intro: This lesson gives the vocabulary for describing a flat and going through the practical steps of renting one: the rooms, what the rent includes, the deposit and the contract.

items.hr: Busco un piso de dos habitaciones en el centro.
items.en: I'm looking for a two-bedroom flat in the centre.

items.hr: El salón es luminoso, pero la cocina es pequeña.
items.en: The living room is bright, but the kitchen is small.

items.hr: El alquiler incluye el agua, pero no incluye la luz.
items.en: The rent includes water, but it doesn't include electricity.

items.hr: Hay que pagar una fianza de un mes antes de firmar el contrato.
items.en: You have to pay a deposit of one month before signing the contract.

items.hr: El piso que vi ayer tiene una terraza que me gusta mucho.
items.en: The flat I saw yesterday has a terrace that I like a lot.

activities.title: Practica el vocabulario de la casa
activities.intro: Practice housing vocabulary and rental structures.

questions.prompt: Elige la palabra correcta: 'Pago el ___ todos los meses al propietario.'
questions.explanation: El alquiler is the monthly rent paid to the propietario, the landlord.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué es la fianza?
options: Una cantidad de dinero que se paga como garantía al empezar el contrato
El dinero que se paga cada mes por vivir en el piso
El documento que firman el propietario y el inquilino
La habitación más grande de la casa
questions.answer: Una cantidad de dinero que se paga como garantía al empezar el contrato
questions.explanation: La fianza is a deposit paid as a guarantee, usually returned at the end of the tenancy.

questions.prompt: El piso tiene tres _____: el salón, la cocina y el baño.
questions.explanation: Habitación can mean any room, not only a bedroom, depending on context.

questions.prompt: Vivo en este piso _____ hace dos años.
questions.explanation: Desde hace + time expresses duration up to now.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Before signing the contract, I want to see the flat again.'
questions.explanation: Antes de + infinitive comes first, since the same person does both actions.

activities.title: Visitando un piso
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Show a flat to a prospective tenant, using housing vocabulary.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Buenos días, vengo a ver el piso que anunciaron.
lines.en: Good morning, I've come to see the flat you advertised.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro, pase. Este es el salón, y al fondo está la cocina.
lines.en: Of course, come in. This is the living room, and the kitchen is at the back.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cuántas habitaciones tiene el piso?
lines.en: How many rooms does the flat have?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tiene dos habitaciones y un baño, y también hay una pequeña terraza.
lines.en: It has two bedrooms and one bathroom, and there's also a small terrace.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿El alquiler incluye los gastos de comunidad?
lines.en: Does the rent include the community fees?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, incluye la comunidad, pero no incluye la luz ni el gas.
lines.en: Yes, it includes the community fees, but it doesn't include electricity or gas.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Perfecto, ¿cuánto es la fianza?
lines.en: Perfect, how much is the deposit?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Un mes de alquiler, y hay que firmar el contrato por un año.
lines.en: One month's rent, and you have to sign the contract for a year.

days.title: Las tareas domésticas
days.objective: The learner can talk about household chores and negotiate sharing them with housemates.
days.paretoFocus: Coordinating chores is a constant real-life need for anyone sharing a flat, and it recycles the imperative and object pronouns in a natural context.
drills: List five household chores in Spanish.
Write a short plan dividing chores between two housemates.
Practise asking who fregar/plancha/barre this week.

items: Recall three words for rooms in a flat.
Recall the phrase pagar una fianza.
Recall how to say the rent includes or doesn't include something.

activities.title: Las tareas domésticas
activities.intro: This lesson gives the vocabulary for household chores and practises negotiating who does what, recycling the imperative, object pronouns and obligation structures already learned.

items.hr: ¿Quién friega los platos hoy? Yo los fregué ayer.
items.en: Who's washing the dishes today? I washed them yesterday.

items.hr: Por favor, saca la basura antes de las nueve.
items.en: Please take out the rubbish before nine.

items.hr: Tenemos que repartir las tareas entre los tres.
items.en: We have to divide the chores between the three of us.

items.hr: ¿Puedes pasar la aspiradora mientras yo plancho?
items.en: Can you vacuum while I iron?

items.hr: Odio fregar los platos, pero me toca a mí esta semana.
items.en: I hate washing the dishes, but it's my turn this week.

activities.title: Practica las tareas domésticas
activities.intro: Practice chore vocabulary and negotiating who does what.

questions.prompt: Elige la tarea correcta para 'to iron the clothes'.
questions.explanation: Planchar means to iron.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué significa 'me toca a mí'?
questions.explanation: Tocar here is used idiomatically for whose turn it is to do something.

questions.prompt: Antes de salir, voy a _____ la basura.
questions.explanation: Sacar la basura means to take out the rubbish.

questions.prompt: No he fregado los platos _____ no he tenido tiempo.
questions.explanation: Porque introduces the cause.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'You can vacuum while I wash the dishes.'
questions.explanation: Mientras introduces a simultaneous action, both verbs stay in the present.

activities.title: Repartiendo las tareas
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two housemates divide the chores.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Este piso está muy desordenado, ¿repartimos las tareas?
lines.en: This flat is very messy, shall we divide the chores?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, yo puedo fregar los platos y sacar la basura.
lines.en: Okay, I can wash the dishes and take out the rubbish.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Genial, entonces yo paso la aspiradora y plancho la ropa.
lines.en: Great, then I'll vacuum and iron the clothes.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: ¿Quién barre la cocina esta semana?
lines.en: Who's sweeping the kitchen this week?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Me toca a mí, la barrí la semana pasada también.
lines.en: It's my turn, I swept it last week too.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, y el sábado tendemos la ropa entre los dos.
lines.en: Okay, and on Saturday we'll hang up the laundry together, the two of us.

days.title: El barrio y la ciudad
days.objective: The learner can describe a neighbourhood, compare it to another and give directions within it.
days.paretoFocus: Describing where things are and how to get there is essential for orienting a new resident or a visitor.
drills: Describe your neighbourhood using hay and está.
Give directions from your home to the nearest shop.
Compare your neighbourhood to another one using más/menos que.

items: Recall three household chores.
Recall how to say whose turn it is to do a chore.
Recall the phrase repartir las tareas.

activities.title: El barrio y la ciudad
activities.intro: This lesson gives the vocabulary for describing a neighbourhood and giving directions within it, recycling hay/estar for location, comparatives and the imperative.

items.hr: En mi barrio hay una plaza muy bonita y dos panaderías.
items.en: In my neighbourhood there's a very pretty square and two bakeries.

items.hr: La farmacia está al lado del banco, enfrente del parque.
items.en: The pharmacy is next to the bank, opposite the park.

items.hr: Este barrio es más tranquilo que el centro.
items.en: This neighbourhood is quieter than the centre.

items.hr: Para llegar a la biblioteca, sigue todo recto y gira a la izquierda.
items.en: To get to the library, go straight ahead and turn left.

items.hr: Antes había menos tráfico en esta calle.
items.en: There used to be less traffic on this street.

activities.title: Practica el barrio
activities.intro: Practice neighbourhood vocabulary, comparatives and directions.

questions.prompt: Elige la traducción correcta de 'opposite the park'.
questions.explanation: Enfrente de means opposite; 'detrás de parque' is missing the required del.

questions.prompt: Elige la instrucción correcta para dar direcciones a un amigo (tú).
options: Gira a la derecha en la plaza.
Gire a la derecha en la plaza.
Giras a la derecha en la plaza.
Girad a la derecha en la plaza.
questions.answer: Gira a la derecha en la plaza.
questions.explanation: The tú imperative of girar is gira; the other forms are usted, present indicative and vosotros.

questions.prompt: Mi barrio es muy tranquilo, hay _____ ruido que en el centro.
questions.explanation: Menos... que forms the comparative of inferiority.

questions.prompt: Voy al ayuntamiento _____ pedir un certificado.
questions.explanation: Para + infinitive expresses purpose.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'There used to be a market on this street, but now there's a car park.'
questions.explanation: Había is the imperfecto of hay, used for descriptions of how things used to be.

activities.title: Cómo es tu barrio
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends describe and compare their neighbourhoods.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cómo es el barrio donde vives ahora?
lines.en: What's the neighbourhood where you live now like?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es muy tranquilo, hay un parque grande y varias tiendas pequeñas.
lines.en: It's very quiet, there's a big park and several small shops.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Hay alguna farmacia cerca de tu casa?
lines.en: Is there a pharmacy near your house?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, hay una farmacia justo enfrente, al lado de la panadería.
lines.en: Yes, there's a pharmacy right opposite, next to the bakery.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y cómo se llega desde tu casa hasta la estación?
lines.en: And how do you get from your house to the station?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sigues todo recto por esta calle y giras a la derecha en la plaza.
lines.en: You go straight ahead along this street and turn right at the square.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Parece un barrio mejor que el mío, allí hay demasiado tráfico.
lines.en: It sounds like a better neighbourhood than mine, there's too much traffic there.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, antes también había más ruido aquí, pero ahora está mucho más tranquilo.
lines.en: Yes, there used to be more noise here too, but now it's much quieter.

days.title: De compras: la ropa
days.objective: The learner can shop for clothes, ask about sizes, try things on and handle a return.
days.paretoFocus: Clothes shopping is a common transactional situation that recycles polite requests and comparatives in a practical setting.
drills: Practise asking for a different size in a shop.
Write a short exchange about trying on clothes.
Practise the polite request ¿Me pone...? in three different situations.

items: Recall how to give directions with the tú imperative.
Recall a comparative sentence about two neighbourhoods.
Recall the imperfecto of hay: había.

activities.title: De compras: la ropa
activities.intro: This lesson gives the vocabulary and polite requests needed to shop for clothes: asking for a size, trying something on and returning an item.

items.hr: ¿Tiene esta camisa en la talla mediana?
items.en: Do you have this shirt in medium size?

items.hr: ¿Me puedo probar estos pantalones?
items.en: Can I try these trousers on?

items.hr: Me quedan un poco grandes, ¿tiene una talla menos?
items.en: They're a bit big on me, do you have a smaller size?

items.hr: Quiero devolver esta chaqueta porque tiene un defecto.
items.en: I want to return this jacket because it has a defect.

items.hr: ¿Me pone el recibo, por favor? Necesito el ticket para devolverlo.
items.en: Could you give me the receipt please? I need the ticket to return it.

activities.title: Practica de compras: la ropa
activities.intro: Practice shopping for clothes, sizes and returns.

questions.prompt: Elige la pregunta correcta para pedir probarte algo.
questions.explanation: Probarse + reflexive pronoun is the natural way to ask about trying something on.

questions.prompt: Elige la opción correcta: 'Estos zapatos me quedan pequeños, ¿tiene una talla ___?'
questions.explanation: Una talla más means a bigger size, one size up.

questions.prompt: Esta camiseta tiene un defecto, quiero _____ el dinero.
questions.explanation: Recuperar el dinero means to get the money back after a return.

questions.prompt: Compré este vestido _____ mi hermana, es su cumpleaños.
questions.explanation: Para marks the recipient of the gift.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Could you give me this jacket in a smaller size, please?'
questions.explanation: ¿Me pone...? is the everyday polite request pattern for asking a shop assistant for something.

activities.title: En la tienda de ropa
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Shop for a shirt, try it on and ask about returns.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Hola, ¿te puedo ayudar en algo?
lines.en: Hi, can I help you with anything?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, busco una camisa para una boda, ¿tiene esta en talla grande?
lines.en: Yes, I'm looking for a shirt for a wedding, do you have this one in a large size?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Sí, aquí tiene. ¿Se la quiere probar?
lines.en: Yes, here you are. Would you like to try it on?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, por favor. ¿Dónde están los probadores?
lines.en: Yes, please. Where are the fitting rooms?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Al fondo a la derecha. Si le queda grande, tenemos una talla menos.
lines.en: At the back on the right. If it's too big on you, we have a smaller size.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, gracias. Y si no me gusta, ¿puedo devolverla otro día?
lines.en: Okay, thanks. And if I don't like it, can I return it another day?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Claro, tiene treinta días con el recibo de compra.
lines.en: Of course, you have thirty days with the purchase receipt.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Perfecto, entonces me la llevo.
lines.en: Perfect, then I'll take it.

days.title: La compra de comida
days.objective: The learner can shop for food using accurate quantity expressions and packaging vocabulary.
days.paretoFocus: Buying food by weight, unit and container is a daily transactional need that A2 listening and speaking tasks specifically test.
drills: List five quantity expressions used in food shopping.
Practise a short dialogue ordering fruit and vegetables.
Practise the polite request ¿Me pone...? for buying food.

items: Recall the polite request pattern used in a clothes shop.
Recall how to ask for a smaller size.
Recall the phrase tiene un defecto.

activities.title: La compra de comida
activities.intro: This lesson gives the quantity expressions and container vocabulary needed to shop for food, recycling the polite request patterns already learned.

items.hr: ¿Me pone medio kilo de tomates, por favor?
items.en: Could you give me half a kilo of tomatoes, please?

items.hr: Quiero una barra de pan y una docena de huevos.
items.en: I want a loaf of bread and a dozen eggs.

items.hr: ¿Tiene leche en botella de cristal o solo en cartón?
items.en: Do you have milk in a glass bottle or only in a carton?

items.hr: Necesito una lata de atún y un paquete de arroz.
items.en: I need a can of tuna and a packet of rice.

items.hr: Compré demasiada fruta y ahora se está poniendo mala.
items.en: I bought too much fruit and now it's going bad.
items.note: estar + gerundio for something happening gradually right now

activities.title: Practica la compra de comida
activities.intro: Practice quantity expressions and containers for food shopping.

questions.prompt: Elige la unidad correcta para huevos.
questions.explanation: Eggs are conventionally sold and asked for by the dozen.

questions.prompt: Elige la frase correcta para pedir en la frutería.
options: ¿Me pone un kilo de naranjas, por favor?
questions.answer: ¿Me pone un kilo de naranjas, por favor?
questions.explanation: De introduces the item after a quantity; por and en are the wrong prepositions here.

questions.prompt: El zumo viene en una _____ de cristal de un litro.
questions.explanation: Botella means bottle, the usual container for juice and milk.

questions.prompt: No _____ dónde está la sección de congelados, voy a preguntar.
questions.explanation: Saber + information.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I need half a kilo of cheese and a packet of pasta.'
questions.explanation: Medio kilo de + noun and un paquete de + noun are the standard quantity patterns.

activities.title: En el mercado
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Shop for food at a market stall, using quantity expressions.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Buenos días, ¿qué le pongo hoy?
lines.en: Good morning, what can I get you today?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Buenos días, quiero medio kilo de patatas y una docena de huevos.
lines.en: Good morning, I'd like half a kilo of potatoes and a dozen eggs.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Muy bien. ¿Algo más? Las fresas están buenísimas esta semana.
lines.en: Very good. Anything else? The strawberries are really good this week.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, me pone también un kilo de fresas, por favor.
lines.en: Yes, give me a kilo of strawberries too, please.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Quiere la leche en botella de cristal o en cartón?
lines.en: Do you want the milk in a glass bottle or in a carton?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Mejor en cartón, es más fácil de llevar.
lines.en: Better in a carton, it's easier to carry.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Aquí tiene todo. Son doce euros con cincuenta.
lines.en: Here's everything. That's twelve euros fifty.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tome, y muchas gracias, todo tiene muy buena pinta.
lines.en: Here you go, and thank you very much, everything looks really good.

days.title: Comer fuera: pedir y pagar
days.objective: The learner can order food in a restaurant, complain politely about a dish, and ask for and settle the bill.
days.paretoFocus: Ordering and paying is the transaction a traveller repeats daily, and it is precisely the kind of simulated exchange the A2 speaking prueba asks for.
drills: Write three lines you would say to order a starter, a main course and a drink.
Practise two different polite ways to ask for the bill.
Say aloud what you would tell a waiter if a dish arrived cold.

items: Recall how to attach an object pronoun to a formal usted command.
Remember a comparative sentence comparing two dishes.
Recall the difference between ser and estar for describing food.

activities.title: En el restaurante
activities.intro: Learn the phrases for ordering food, describing a problem with a dish, and asking for and paying the bill.

items.hr: ¿Nos trae la carta, por favor?
items.en: Could you bring us the menu, please?
items.note: A polite request in the present tense, not the imperative.

items.hr: De primero quiero la ensalada, y de segundo, el pescado.
items.en: For a starter I'll have the salad, and for a main, the fish.

items.hr: Perdone, esto está muy frío. ¿Me lo puede cambiar?
items.en: Excuse me, this is very cold. Can you change it for me?
items.note: lo is the direct object pronoun, attached after puede.

items.hr: ¿Nos trae la cuenta, por favor? Pagamos por separado.
items.en: Could you bring us the bill, please? We're paying separately.

items.hr: ¿Aceptan tarjeta o solo efectivo?
items.en: Do you take card, or only cash?

activities.title: Pedir y pagar
activities.intro: Practise the language of ordering, complaining politely and paying.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué dices si la comida está fría y quieres que te la cambien?
options: Esto está muy frío. ¿Me lo puede cambiar?
Esto está muy frío. ¿Te lo puedo cambiar?
Esto está muy frío. ¿Me los puede cambiar?
questions.answer: Esto está muy frío. ¿Me lo puede cambiar?
questions.explanation: Me is the speaker asking for themselves, lo is singular for the one dish, and puede is the formal usted form for a stranger; the other options swap the pronoun person, break the verb agreement, or use the wrong pronoun number.

questions.prompt: ¿Cómo pides la cuenta de manera educada a un camarero que no conoces?
questions.explanation: A request to a stranger uses usted in the present; vosotros addresses people you know informally as a group, and the past tenses cannot form a request.

questions.prompt: Completa: Perdone, ¿nos ______ la carta, por favor? (traer, usted)
questions.explanation: Formal request with usted in the present tense.

questions.prompt: Completa: El pescado está más barato ______ la carne hoy. (than)
questions.explanation: que follows más or menos in a comparison.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Do you take card, or only cash?'
questions.explanation: Aceptan is the plural form used for a business, and o solo introduces the alternative.

activities.title: Una mesa para dos
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Send back a dish that isn't right, then flag down the waiter to pay up.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Buenas tardes, ¿qué van a tomar?
lines.en: Good afternoon, what will you have?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: De primero, la ensalada, y de segundo, el pescado, por favor.
lines.en: For a starter, the salad, and for a main, the fish, please.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Muy bien. ¿Y para beber?
lines.en: Very good. And to drink?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Agua con gas, por favor.
lines.en: Sparkling water, please.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Aquí tiene, el pescado.
lines.en: Here you are, the fish.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Perdone, esto está muy frío. ¿Me lo puede cambiar?
lines.en: Excuse me, this is very cold. Can you change it for me?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Claro, lo siento mucho. Se lo cambio ahora mismo.
lines.en: Of course, I'm very sorry. I'll change it for you right now.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Gracias. Y al final, ¿nos trae la cuenta? Pagamos por separado.
lines.en: Thanks. And finally, could you bring us the bill? We're paying separately.

days.title: El cuerpo y los síntomas
days.objective: The learner can name body parts, describe symptoms and say what hurts using doler.
days.paretoFocus: Describing how you feel is essential for any health situation, and doler follows the same pattern as gustar that the learner already knows.
drills: Point to five body parts and say their names aloud.
Say three symptoms using tener plus a noun.
Say what hurts today using me duele or me duelen.

items: Recall how gustar agrees with a singular or plural thing that is liked.
Remember the perfecto for something that has happened today.
Recall estar plus an adjective for a temporary state.

activities.title: El cuerpo y los síntomas
activities.intro: Learn the main body parts and how to describe a symptom, including doler, which agrees with the thing that hurts, not with the person.

items.hr: Me duele la cabeza desde esta mañana.
items.en: My head has been hurting since this morning.
items.note: doler works like gustar: me duele + singular, me duelen + plural.

items.hr: Me duelen las piernas después de correr.
items.en: My legs hurt after running.

items.hr: Tengo fiebre y mucha tos.
items.en: I have a fever and a bad cough.

items.hr: Estoy resfriado y me duele la garganta.
items.en: I have a cold and my throat hurts.

items.hr: Ayer estuve mareado todo el día.
items.en: Yesterday I was dizzy all day.
items.note: estuve, indefinido of estar, for a completed state.

activities.title: ¿Qué te duele?
activities.intro: Practise describing symptoms and using doler correctly.

questions.prompt: ¿Cómo se dice correctamente 'my legs hurt'?
questions.explanation: piernas is plural, so the verb must be duelen, and me matches the speaker; the other options break the plural agreement or use the wrong pronoun.

questions.prompt: Ana tiene mucha temperatura. ¿Qué le pasa?
questions.explanation: fiebre is the word for a raised temperature caused by illness.

questions.prompt: Completa: Me ______ la cabeza. (doler, para 'me')
questions.explanation: The singular subject la cabeza takes the singular form duele.

questions.prompt: Completa, con el verbo en el tiempo correcto para 'ayer': ______ mareado todo el día. (estar, yo, indefinido)
questions.explanation: estuve is the strong-stem indefinido of estar, for a completed state yesterday.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'My throat hurts a lot.'
questions.explanation: duele agrees with the singular la garganta; mucho intensifies the verb.

activities.title: No me encuentro bien
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Describe your symptoms to a friend.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué te pasa? Tienes mala cara.
lines.en: What's wrong? You look unwell.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Me duele mucho la cabeza y tengo un poco de fiebre.
lines.en: My head hurts a lot and I have a slight fever.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Te duele algo más?
lines.en: Does anything else hurt?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, también me duele la garganta y tengo tos.
lines.en: Yes, my throat also hurts and I have a cough.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Parece un resfriado. ¿Estás mareado también?
lines.en: It sounds like a cold. Are you dizzy too?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Un poco, sí. Estuve mareado toda la mañana.
lines.en: A little, yes. I was dizzy all morning.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tienes que descansar y beber mucha agua.
lines.en: You have to rest and drink lots of water.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, voy a quedarme en casa hoy.
lines.en: Yes, I'm going to stay home today.

days.title: Encantar, interesar, molestar, parecer, apetecer
days.objective: The learner can use encantar, interesar, molestar, parecer and apetecer with the same dative pattern as gustar and doler.
days.paretoFocus: This family of verbs works backwards from English, and mastering the full set lets the learner express opinions and preferences naturally in daily conversation.
drills: Say one thing that te encanta and one that te molesta.
Ask a friend ¿Te apetece...? with three different activities.
Say what te parece a plan using me parece plus an adjective.

items: Recall the dative pronouns me, te, le, nos, os, les.
Remember how doler agrees with a singular or plural noun.
Recall a sentence with gustar and a plural noun.

activities.title: Encantar, interesar, molestar, parecer, apetecer
activities.intro: These verbs follow the same backwards pattern as gustar: the person affected takes a dative pronoun, and the verb agrees with the thing that causes the feeling.

items.hr: Me encanta la comida española.
items.en: I love Spanish food.
items.note: encantar, stronger than gustar.

items.hr: Nos interesan mucho las noticias.
items.en: We're very interested in the news.
items.note: interesar agrees with the plural noticias.

items.hr: Me molesta el ruido por la noche.
items.en: Noise at night bothers me.

items.hr: ¿Qué te parece este restaurante?
items.en: What do you think of this restaurant?
items.note: parecer plus an adjective: me parece caro, me parece bien.

items.hr: ¿Te apetece un café ahora?
items.en: Do you fancy a coffee now?
items.note: apetecer, very common in everyday Spanish for offering something.

activities.title: Me encanta, te apetece
activities.intro: Practise the full gustar-class family.

questions.prompt: ¿Cómo dices que te interesan mucho las cosas antiguas?
questions.explanation: cosas antiguas is plural, so interesar agrees: interesan, with me for the speaker.

questions.prompt: Preguntas a un amigo si quiere un café. ¿Qué dices?
questions.explanation: Asking a friend uses te, and café is singular so the verb is apetece; le would address a third person, not the friend in front of you.

questions.prompt: Completa: A mis padres ______ mucho el cine. (encantar, ellos)
questions.explanation: les is the indirect pronoun for ellos, and encanta agrees with the singular el cine.

questions.prompt: Completa: ¿Qué te ______ este plan? (parecer)
questions.explanation: parecer agrees with the singular este plan.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'The noise bothers me a lot.'
questions.explanation: molesta agrees with the singular el ruido.

activities.title: ¿Qué te apetece hacer?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk about plans using the full gustar-class family.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Te apetece salir esta tarde?
lines.en: Do you fancy going out this afternoon?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, me encanta la idea. ¿Qué te parece ir al parque?
lines.en: Yes, I love the idea. What do you think of going to the park?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Me parece bien, pero me molesta el calor a estas horas.
lines.en: Sounds good to me, but the heat bothers me at this time.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es verdad. A mí también me molesta.
lines.en: True. It bothers me too.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y si vamos al cine? Me interesa mucho la película nueva.
lines.en: What if we go to the cinema? I'm very interested in the new film.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Perfecto, me encantan las películas de aventuras.
lines.en: Perfect, I love adventure films.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Nos vemos a las seis, entonces?
lines.en: Shall we meet at six, then?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, nos vemos a las seis.
lines.en: Okay, see you at six.

days.title: En la consulta y en la farmacia
days.objective: The learner can describe symptoms to a doctor, understand simple instructions, and ask for something at the pharmacy.
days.paretoFocus: Explaining a symptom and understanding an instruction is essential language for living or travelling anywhere, independent of any specific treatment.
drills: Practise saying three symptoms to a doctor using tengo and me duele.
Say two instructions a doctor might give, using the usted imperative.
Ask a pharmacist for something for a headache.

items: Recall the formal usted imperative of an -ar verb.
Remember how to attach a pronoun to a formal command.
Recall the indefinido of ir, for saying 'I went'.

activities.title: En la consulta
activities.intro: Learn how to describe a symptom to a doctor and understand the formal instructions a doctor gives back, using the usted imperative already learned.

items.hr: Buenos días, ¿qué le pasa?
items.en: Good morning, what's wrong?
items.note: the doctor addresses the patient with usted.

items.hr: Me duele mucho el estómago desde ayer.
items.en: My stomach has been hurting a lot since yesterday.

items.hr: Tome esta receta y vaya a la farmacia.
items.en: Take this prescription and go to the pharmacy.
items.note: tome and vaya, formal usted imperatives.

items.hr: Descanse unos días y beba mucha agua.
items.en: Rest for a few days and drink lots of water.

items.hr: ¿Tiene algo para el dolor de cabeza?
items.en: Do you have something for a headache?
items.note: asked at the pharmacy counter.

activities.title: Instrucciones del médico
activities.intro: Practise understanding a doctor's instructions and asking at the pharmacy.

questions.prompt: El médico te da una instrucción formal para descansar. ¿Cuál es?
questions.explanation: The formal usted imperative is descanse; descansa is the informal tú imperative, and the other two are past tenses, not commands.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué preguntas en la farmacia si te duele la cabeza?
options: ¿Tiene algo para el dolor de cabeza?
questions.answer: ¿Tiene algo para el dolor de cabeza?
questions.explanation: The symptom named must match the question: a headache needs something for el dolor de cabeza.

questions.prompt: Completa con el imperativo formal: ______ esta receta y vaya a la farmacia. (tomar, usted)
questions.explanation: Tome is the usted imperative of tomar, from the yo-stem.

questions.prompt: Completa: Ayer ______ al médico porque me dolía mucho el estómago. (ir, yo, indefinido)
questions.explanation: fui is the indefinido of ir.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Rest for a few days and drink lots of water.'
